review_1_text:
The waterfall is amazing and the thermal pools are really nice too, the food is decent too.
Couple of negative points though:
You can only enter 3 specific times a day, 6am, 11am, 6pm. If you arrive at 4pm, you'll have to wait 2 hours.
The prices on the website are cheaper than buying them at the ticket office, but you still need to go to the ticket office to get a wristband.
Even after paying the high ticket price you need to spend 2000 pesos to get access to a locker, for which you need to queue 15 minutes for.
The pools get very packed when I went, at the 6pm session.
There are no hot showers for when you want to leave.
If you go for the 6pm session, ensure you organise some sort of transport since the buses to Santa Rosa stop at 7pm.

There's nothing more enchanting for a Vietnamese Gringo to experience this masterpiece etched by the Colombian Gods.

Los Arrieros is a nice little restaurant with a lovely view, situation on the side of a mountain.  It's only possible to pull into the parking lot while you're on the way up, unfortunately, so if you want to stop in while you're on the way down you'll need to turnaround, and the nearest place to do so isn't very nearby.  This isn't the fault of the establishment, just something worth pointing out.

The food is the traditional Colombian style: farm beans, steak, plantains, fish, and the like.  I tried the baby beef and it was fantastic.  I ordered beans with aguacate for my boys and they loved it.  Everything we tried was very good.

Service was good, but no English so be prepared.  The view is great, and everything was clean, including the restrooms.

If you're looking for traditional Colombian food with a nice view, Los Arrieros is a great choice.  Definitely recommend!

The call of Padre Yagé led me on a quest to find the perfect sanctuary for my first yagé experience. I was determined to avoid falling into the trap of commercialization, where I might find myself surrounded by dozens of tourists in a sterile, impersonal setting, all at exorbitant prices.

Seeking an authentic yagé ceremony guided by experienced shamans, I stumbled upon Martha's Instagram profile. From our initial conversation to meeting them in person, my experience with them was nothing short of exceptional. They expressed warmth, empathy, and profound wisdom.

Throughout the sessions, Martha had an innate sense of when to provide guidance and support, and when to allow me to navigate my journey independently. I loved our conversations on the next day about my journey (and their journeys as well).

Both Juan and Martha not only made my experience unforgettable but also offered unique perspectives on the yagé ceremony.

It's evident that they are deeply passionate about their work, sharing the love and wisdom of yagé with wholehearted dedication.

Although the current ceremony location is simple and rustic (which I personally found to be authentic and charming), they have embarked on a new project that promises to be truly remarkable and beneficial for many more individuals.

Martha and Juan, I am immensely grateful for the life-changing experience you facilitated and the love you shared with me. I eagerly anticipate returning to witness the unfolding of your new project.

Hasta pronto amigos :)
Jörg

review_1_text: For those who visit it: it is a space for environmental conservation. Please do not leave garbage and DO NOT contaminate its waters. If possible, do not go with children or animals. A lovely place. Small trail that allows you to cross a beautiful ravine several times in the middle of the dry tropical forest. Home to many birds and small mammals.

review_1_text:
Great place to be. We stayed for 5 days and enjoyed being surrounded by nature. Very nice being part of the Tio Conejo Family. Coffee picking, tasting and learning about the challenges in the coffee world.
Great cooking together and great food. It was amazing.
review_2_text:
Best coffee experience I've ever had! From the beginning of the tour you get an amazing view with a cup of their original coffee. During the tour you get to walk through the coffee fields and explore more of their terrain. They have room for people that want to stay the night in the fields, which I will definitely come back to do! Also, thank you to Santiago for giving us the history and stages of how coffee is produced and all their different agriculture produced on their land. The terrain is intermediate on some areas, but Santiago was very patient and careful with us making sure we were always good. After walking the fields, the tour includes a very delicious meal made with products produced on their land. We had pumpkin soup, roasted vegetables, and pasta with ground meat. After dinner, we had another more in-depth of how the different grains taste like after being brewed and the different ways to enjoy coffee in the brewing making. Honestly, if I can give this spot more than 5 stars, I would!

Only downfall is getting there, it is a steep hill and the entrance is even steeper. So take that in consideration with the vehicle you are driving with to get in. But don't let this sway you away, it's definitely a great experience to have!
review_3_text:
We have such good memories from our stay at Tio Conejo.
We were looking for a small place to stay. I am interested in birding and we were also looking to do a coffee tour in a small coffee farm.
This place appeared to have everything we were looking for. From the beginning, the communication and planning was excellent.
We had the coffee tour, coffee tasting, lodging, food, overnight stay and a birding tour in the morning, all at the same place.  We highly recommend!
review_4_text: Stayed 1 night as a group of 4. Accommodations were nice, views amazing. The dinner, and other meals prepared by the owners for me was the best part. My friends are into coffee but I didn't care much for it. Its a small farm so doesn't take long to complete the tour.
review_5_text: One of the best authentic experiences I've done on my life. Day starts with your of coffee plantation but Ivanov explains how he decided to make it sustainable from an environmental, social and economic basis. This is a must see for anyone interested in more than just a quick visit to see crops and a coffee gift shop.

review_1_text:
The room is spacious with walls of windows overlooking the forest and thermal springs.
Bathroom is nice and modern.
Nevertheless maybe the room is too insulated because if you're not opening the windows it gets very foggy instantly.
The staff is meh, I had to speak to literally everyone walking around to get checked-in and pay hotel & restaurant to different people, quite annoying...
If you're staying at the hotel you can enjoy the pools but also private little bath with a table and chairs, really really nice!
review_2_text:
There was nobody at the reception, then one guy show us were the rooms were. Then back to the reception to pay for the room and then bring us to the actual room. They were doing some renovation so some part of the stairs were not practicable. Also painters were just outside our room windows in the morning. The pools closes at midnight and we could hear the music until late.
BUT the room was very clean, spacious and the bed very comfortable, the best mattress and pillow we got so far in Colombia (9 nights for now).
The private little termal bath was very hot but nice.
The food and beverage were very good and tasty! We got the veggies burger, some home made juice and the breakfast was good as well.
review_3_text: A treasure found not so far from the main city with its quiet surroundings filled with beautiful trees, flowers and plants,  you can easily spend hours or days here in complete peace and quiet that we all need.  Food and service equally great!  will definitely visit again with friends and family!  Thank you!
review_4_text: The rooms are very nice and spacious and each one has a small jacuzzi thermal spring outside for you to use privately. You can also use the big thermal pools as well. The road it’s on passes by some factories, so you would think it’s not going to be a nice place, but it is.
review_5_text:
We stayed at Isabel’s finca in Santa Rosa de Cabal last Saturday as a base to visit the nearby termales, and it was a perfect choice. Isabel was incredibly warm and hospitable—she even helped us plan our visit to Termales San Vicente, which made everything smoother.

The finca itself was cozy, peaceful, and ideally located for exploring the hot springs in the area. Our room was clean, well equipped, and we slept very comfortably.

A special bonus was the presence of many adorable and friendly animals—dogs, cats, pigs, ducks, and even a hen—which made the experience even more memorable. Highly recommend if you’re looking for a tranquil, welcoming stay in the region.

review_1_text:
This hotel feels like it was plucked straight out of a fairy tale! The views are absolutely breathtaking, and the rooms are cozy and well-equipped. I especially loved the heater, private jacuzzi, and sauna in my room—it made the stay feel luxurious and relaxing.

A few things to keep in mind:
- The **day pool pass** is available on a **first-come, first-served basis**, so plan accordingly if you want to enjoy the pool during the day.
- The **more scenic pools** are exclusive to hotel guests, meaning you **must be a guest at the hotel** to access them. This makes the experience feel more private and special, but it’s something to note if you’re considering a day visit.

The food, while delicious, felt a bit overpriced. However, I understand that the remote location might contribute to the higher costs. Speaking of location, the last 10 kilometers to the hotel were a bit rough, so I highly recommend following the staff’s directions carefully to make the journey smoother.

Most of the staff went above and beyond to make our stay enjoyable, but I did find some of the front desk personnel to be less welcoming, which was a bit disappointing. Additionally, after 10 PM, everything shuts down, including the front desk, and you can only contact the emergency number for medical issues. The internet also became practically unusable after 10 PM, so plan accordingly if you need connectivity late at night.

Despite these minor drawbacks, the overall experience was fantastic. The stunning views, luxurious amenities, and attentive service from most of the staff made it a memorable stay. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a peaceful, fairy-tale-like getaway—just be prepared for the remote location and a few quirks.
review_2_text: Absolutely stunning! The best hotel I’ve stayed at in Colombia for this budget. Wonderful landscapes, amazing thermal waters, fresh weather and a cherry on top - their chef does magic! Truly delicious cuisine! Will definitely come back
review_3_text:
This was a mixed experience for us. We didn’t feel entirely welcome as foreigners here and some of the staff were cool if not unfriendly. I think it’s worth staying the night to make use of the nicer pools and lounging areas. Most everyone who was there for the day had cleared out by 4 and we enjoyed the last two hours which were more peaceful. It was challenging driving down that road in the dark, though!

name: Termales El Sifón
review_1_text:
I was there in the dia ferrada. A lot of people wanted to go in and we had to wait a while. It was a little chaos but just because a lot of cars 😄
In the termales byself there was not too mich people. I expected more people because the holi/y-days 😋
The water is super warm but you will find a spot where the water is perfect temperature for you (the further down you go the colder it gets)
The best is to go with a rented bike or car there. From manizales, murillo or libano. The way to the entry of the termales (15‘000) is with normal streets and drivable in every weather. If the weather is dry, the way down to the termales is possible with every bike and i would say even with every car. But at least with EVERY bike. If its rainy i would just go with cars and bikes with enough power and grip because gravelroad and sometimes a bit steep.
By foot you need around 30-40min one way from the entry to the termales.
You don‘t need a guide.
If you go by jeep the offer from murillo was 150k per person.

If you‘re not sure…just do it
Its worth it

review_1_text:
The place is really amazing. Breathtaking. The waterfalls and the little river crossing around make the visit already worth it.

We went early in the morning and it was not so crowded. At 11am got really crowded.

The pools are not really taking care of. They need a bit more of maintenance. For the amount of money they charge you would expect something better.

People goes inside with clothes and drinks. There are signs with rules but Nobody from the place is controlling them. It is a bit disgusting.

Overall this place is fine, worth the visit just for the place, not for the termales.

Tip: buy the tickets in advance as they are cheaper. But you will still need to queue to get the brazaletes.

review_2_text:
My stay at Termales Santa Rosa de Cabal was nothing short of magical, a true escape into a world of relaxation, natural beauty, and rejuvenation. Nestled in the heart of the Colombian mountains, this paradise blends breathtaking landscapes, healing thermal waters, and top tier service into an experience that feels like stepping into a dream.

From the moment I arrived, I was welcomed with warm hospitality and impeccable service that made me feel like a valued guest. The staff was incredibly attentive, ensuring every detail of my stay was perfect. Whether it was guiding me through the resort, recommending the best pools for relaxation, or simply greeting me with a smile, their dedication was unmatched.

The thermal pools are the highlight of this oasis, offering a unique blend of warm, mineral rich waters that naturally relax the body and rejuvenate the soul. Surrounded by lush green mountains and the soothing sounds of waterfalls, every soak felt like a healing ritual. The contrast between the cool mountain air and the steaming pools created an invigorating sensation that left me feeling completely refreshed.

Beyond the pools, Termales Santa Rosa de Cabal offers a complete sensory experience. The on site spa takes relaxation to the next level, with massages and treatments that melt away stress. The restaurant serves exquisite local cuisine, with fresh flavors that perfectly complement the natural surroundings. And for those who love adventure, there are hiking trails leading to stunning waterfalls, where nature reveals its most breathtaking wonders.

What truly sets this place apart is the energy, there is something about the combination of the pristine environment, the healing waters, and the warm hospitality that makes this destination feel almost sacred. It is a place where stress disappears, the body is renewed, and the mind finds clarity.

Termales Santa Rosa de Cabal is not just a getaway, it is an experience that stays with you long after you leave. Whether you are seeking relaxation, adventure, or a deep connection with nature, this place delivers it all. I left feeling recharged, inspired, and already planning my next visit.
review_3_text: Wow. A secret paradise of waterfalls and tranquility in the Colombian mountains. Amazing food and drinks as well as spa and outdoor experience. Stay an extra day to experience it all.  Book Room 210 and experience a beautiful view and the peaceful sound of the waterfalls at night.

review_1_text: One of the most pleasant hot springs in the country. The place is amazing, you can have a really good time there. We bought the Vital passport that included transport and a full day of the experience + lunch. We had a super relaxing experience, the only downside was that the guests (people staying the night) almost never wore face masks and that was supposed to be mandatory. We wore them whenever we were out of the hotsprings, unless we were walking along for example
review_2_text: This has to be the best hot springs in Colombia. It is big, with different types of pools to enjoy some hotter than others but hot all the same. The hotel rooms are comfortable but at night it can get really cold in those rooms. This has to be a downside to the place, it could do with some heating. The food is quite good and the service is also good. Access to the place can be complicated it is really far up the mountain and most of the road is off road. But all together a must visit place.
review_3_text: Beautiful experience,  beautiful place!!!
review_4_text: This place is a must try in the region. Expect a local atmosphere, beautiful natural views on top of the mountain (climb the stairs next to the changing rooms), three interconnected “pools” from very hot to a bit warm. The food is very good and quite local (expect a lot of meat). Try the parrillada (a mix of different meat). I would not recommend staying over for the night at the hotel though; its quite old. I recommend booking private transport to get there and to wait for you until you are done. I usually spend 3 hours there. The place is fit for kids. On the way back, try “chorizo santa rosano” on the main square of the town.
review_5_text: Beautiful place , relaxing but lord have mercy...getting there raises your blood pressure!   Its so far n pray your car does not break down!

review_4_text: I absolutely loved my stay in Las Camelias, having stumbled upon it quite by chance. It is a small family run finca (farm) a few minutes walk outside Salento, and offers simple, comfortable accommodation in the form of dorms, private rooms, or tents (aka glamping). The owner is really hospitable and friendly, and made me feel at home and part of the family from the very beginning (of course it probably helped that I can speak Spanish!). She prepares a simple, fresh and tasty breakfast of omelette, fruit, bread and coffee in the morning. I really feel like she makes a lot of effort to make her hostel a great place to stay, creating a genuine and down-to-earth environment. You are surrounded by nature (horses, cows, ducks and fireflies, not to mention beautiful views of the countryside) and it is the perfect environment to relax for a few days, with the advantage of being a quick walk into town. I don’t usually bother to write reviews for hostels but I really wanted to for Las Camelias as I feel a lot of gratitude; I wish the owner every success for the future :-)

Painted in yellow, green, orange, and violet, they give the impression that they're watching over the park. review_1_text: This is a must if you’re staying in Filandia! It’s not commonly in the tourist guides so you have to look for it but this was the perfect experience. Luis the guide doesn’t speak English but is really good at communicating important info. We’re not fluent in Spanish but got 90% of what he was saying. The fauna is wonderful and surprisingly close to Filandia. We were super lucky and got to see monkeys right away from very close including a mother and her baby. It was super special. Bear in mind that in 20% of cases, you won’t see monkeys. But the hike is beautiful. The 3 hours flew by. Bring strong mosquito repellent (like Nopikex) because you’ll be in the middle of the jungle! Meet the guide directly at their office, it’s easier than having to look for them in the Plaza.
review_2_text: Luis was an amazing guide! We saw howler monkeys, poison dart frogs, centipedes and lot more. Highly recommend this trip to Reserva Bremen
review_3_text:
Unfortunately, I wouldn’t recommend. They take you through the pastures of some fincas and then about 10-15 minutes into the jungle to a waterfall. It is not the actual Barbas Bremen reserve. I did not see an Howler Monkeys, which I understand can happen, but the walk itself really wasn’t all that great. You want to go to Yarumal to DCS Sendero Barbas Bremen

Don Luis is kind but this felt like a tourist trap.
review_4_text: We didn't see the monkeys, but this is not the main issue - we knew it would be hard to. The thing that left me disappointed is that it was not a guided tour, unless guiding means walking at full speed in front of a group of 12 people without explaining anything of what you have around except "don't touch this tree". I am used to walk in the mountains and had proper equipment, but they accept anyone and in our group there were people with regular sneakers and a very young girl at her first hiking experience. The path is quite muddy and often gets steep and they were struggling. In the end the guide was in a great hurry to get back to meet the jeep and put pressure on the girl who was drinking some water. But there was time dedicated to take dozens of pictures of the "highlight" of the hike - a small waterfall like many you can see walking by yourself anywhere in the forest around Quindio. I am also not sure we were really in the Bremen Reserve as their poster states, since my friend's gps located us outside of the reserve on Google maps, quite far on the opposite side of the Rio, and we entered the wood through a tiny fenced path without any board or sign with the name of the Reserve like shown on the photos of the Rural Adventures tour we had booked. Not even sure it was the same tour we booked since the reviews tell about very different perks we didn t have (binocoles, coffee, a guide called Alejandro who explains a lot about plants insects and birds...). We felt like really stupid tourists who fell in a trap and it was sad since it was our last day in Filandia and we couldn't replan a proper tour in the actual Reserve and we probably won't be back in the region ever again. Avoid unless you are prepared and equipped for a muddy hike and you only care about a small chance of seeing an ape far away and nothing more. If you want to hike in the jungle you can make the Valle del cocora loop hike by yourself and see a much more exciting jungle with birds and colibris.
review_5_text: If I could give less than one star for this, I would. It was a trek in the jungle, and that's about it. Nothing was shared about the monkeys, no information on the flora and fauna we encountered, which should have been essential considering monkeys are a plus and seeing them is a matter of luck. I left the tour having learnt nothing new, after an expensive trek I could have done by myself. I'm still not sure we were even in the real Barbas Bremen Reserve, as my gps showed otherwise the whole time and we had to go through barbed wire to get in. Avoid

opening_hours: Monday: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM|Tuesday: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM|Wednesday: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM|Thursday: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM|Friday: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM|Saturday: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM|Sunday: Closed
review_1_text: We really enjoyed this coffee tour. Sabrina was a great guide and gave us real insight into her family's coffee farm and the overall production process. She took us round the coffee farm and at the end, we tried some of the coffee that they grow. It was delicious. It was one of the best tours we've done on our travels. She also has the cutest dogs as well who came along on the tour aswell. I highly recommend this tour if you're interested in an authentic coffee tour experience whilst you're in Salento.
review_2_text:
We had an amazing experience on the Don Eduardo coffee tour in Salento with our fantastic guide, Santiago. The tour was incredibly personal and intimate — Santiago took his time to explain every step of the coffee process, from the plantation and harvesting to the drying, roasting, and brewing. His passion and knowledge made the whole experience even more special.

It’s a truly authentic and educational deep dive into the world of Colombian coffee, far from the crowded touristy feel of other tours. One heads-up: there are quite a lot of mosquitos, so make sure to wear repellent. But overall, this tour is a must-do in Salento — highly recommended!
review_3_text:
"Savrina was the best and most professional guide! With a deep love for Colombia’s nature and animals, she explained the entire coffee process from start to finish in just three hours. She was incredibly patient, took me around the farm, and even shared insights about other plants. She’s truly a wonderful person, and if you’re looking for someone knowledgeable and passionate, don’t hesitate to book this tour!"
I genuinely and wholeheartedly recommend her!"
review_4_text: Great experience! We did three different coffee farm tours in Salento and this one gave the best background/origin and a really authentic experience. Sabrina was wonderful, super friendly and answered lots of questions we had. The meet point is really close to the town centre so you can easily just walk over. You’ll spend the first part learning about coffee and the process before then walking over to the farm (just a few minutes away). The farm itself is a very small operation rather than anything on a commercial scale but you can still parts of the process such as the trees, the pulping, drying etc. After the farm visit you’ll come back and learn how to do basic roasting of the coffee, prepare it, and then drink! Overall the tour lasted about 3 hours and would recommend!
review_5_text: Excellent tour given by Joe. He was extremely knowledgeable on all things coffee, the history, the production process, the nuances of exportation and of course how to make the perfect cuppa. We found the structure very engaging as there were lots of interactive elements, including a tour of the lovely farm! The coffee we hand made at the end was so delicious that we had to buy two bags of beans. Genuinely one of the best tours we have done on our travels so cannot recommend enough!

review_5_text: Unique and super fascinating experiences I would repeat without a doubt as many times as possible, not only do you get to know new places and have a connection with nature but you are surrounded by pleasant and magical people

name: Rural Adventure
review_1_text: Christian and David gave us a marvellous tour of the whole chocolate growing process and we ended up drinking chocolate we had ground ourselves. A bonus is the beautiful setting, humming birds finches, carpenter birds and lots of other exotic plants. Very much recommended !
review_2_text: The experience of going up the Nevado del Ruiz was absolutely magical, one of the highlights of our trip. The communication with Rural Adventures was super efficient and the price very competitive. Nora was a fantastic, kind and knowledgeable guide! 100% recommended 😊
review_3_text: Our tour was fantastic, and our guide, Juan David, was the best. We brought our 5 year old daughter on the tour, and it was very challenging, but Juan David went beyond expectation and assisted her through the hardest parts of the trail. We saw howler monkeys, waterfalls, and even a venemous coral snake. It was a top highlight of our travels in Colombia.
review_4_text: We did the howler monkey tour in Barbas Bremen reserve. It was a beautiful place full of life. Our guide was amazing and very knowledgeable. We saw the beautiful red howler monkeys which was amazing! And finished the trip at a beautiful waterfall. Totally worth it!
review_5_text: Fantastic coffee tour! We got to visit a small farm that is run by one person, which made the tour feel very down to earth. He let us into his house, shared his home made desserts and showed how coffee is grown as well as how it is processed. The tour is very authentic and feels like visiting a friend! You can't go wrong with this tour!

name: Coffee Tour La Palma
review_1_text: I took this tour in September 2024.  I had originally planned a tour from Salento but missed the opportunity and I'm glad I did because I was able to take this tour with Julian.  This is a small private tour and very personalized.  Julian is an excellent host and very knowledgeable about coffee production.  We were able to see his small production up close and he explained everything expertly. The tour was capped with coffee tasting and the various ways to make a perfect up of coffee.  Keep some space in your baggage for a few packages of his excellent coffee beans.
review_2_text:
I really spontaneously booked that tour and I have to say it was great!
Julian our guide took a lot of time and effort explaining us the process of the coffee production and the economy behind it.
The whole tour was super organised and you got to make your own coffee and try it in three different ways.
The finca was really lovely and you can definitely see the effort that is behind that tour
I can highly recommend doing it!!!
review_3_text:
Unforgettable Coffee Tour in Filandia ☕️
This was one of the best experiences we had in Colombia. The tour was intimate and personal, led by a fourth-generation coffee maker who hand-picks every bean on their organic farm. You get to see the full life cycle of coffee—from plant to cup—and it completely changes how you think about buying coffee. We strongly recommend visiting before you buy any other coffee—it’s eye-opening. Filandia is a beautiful town, and taking the time to visit this Finca is absolutely worth it. Buy directly if you can, and don’t be shy—they’ll tell you amazing stories about the town, the plants, the animals, and the history of it all. Truly a must-do!
review_4_text:
This was an excellent coffee tour.
Julian provided interesting information about his family farm and how they use permaculture (not pesticides) to grow their coffee beans. He showed us the farm, how they make compost, how they roast the beans etc.
Julian demonstrated some excellent tips about ways to make the perfect coffee at home, and we tried different methods such as tasted different.
It was such an interesting and informative tour and Julian really brought it to life.
We would highly recommended this tour, particularly as it was a small family business that had such integrity for their product as well as the environment. You can also buy the coffee which was good value.
review_5_text: Incredible coffee tour! Family owned and super authentic. Amazing organic coffee made in a permaculture farm. You will learn so much about coffee while diving into the experience from beginning to end. Juliano is a super informative and friendly guide!

review_1_text: We did the tour this morning and it was the best thing we did in Finlandia! Highly recommended! Agua Bonita is a family-run coffee farm. If you want a factory tour, go to the Parque del Cafe or one of the other tours that show up in your Google search, but if you are interested in learning from and interacting with the actual cafeteros who grow, harvest, process, and make the coffee, this place is for you! Learn about how the family has overcome  a fungus that nearly wiped out their farm and how they rebuilt after a hailstorm that killed their coffee plants. We performed each step of the coffee production process: picking the beans, removing the four layers of skin through grinding, fermentation and drying, and finally brewed our own coffee. This tour is unforgettable!
review_2_text: Really lovely family owned farm. We got a very nice tour and all the questions asked. They really know their business.
review_3_text: Great family-run business to learn about coffee growing & production.
review_4_text:
We loved this tour! I went with my family (five people), and at the same time they taught us, they involved us in the entire coffee-making process! 🧡 From the harvest to the cup. What we liked most was that they revived traditional production processes (without so many machines) and that it's a family business (our guide is a family member). Definitely a must-see tour if you're in Filandia or the area.

Many thanks and congratulations to the Agua Bonita team from Mexico 🇲🇽! 🙌🏽🫶🏽

review_1_text: It has very nice social spaces, the pool is very nice, there are many birds and other animals, I even had the opportunity to see a capybara.
review_2_text:
The estate has a unique style, simple yet charming. From its design to the decorative details, everything is designed to provide comfort and harmony. You feel at home from the moment you arrive.

Regarding the flow of people, it's clear that the estate is in high demand for rentals. This is no surprise, as it offers spacious grounds, a pool, and green areas to enjoy. It's a perfect place to hold events or simply spend an amazing weekend.

Finally, I should mention that although the location is excellent and easily accessible, the rental cost can be a bit high. However, if you're willing to invest in an unforgettable experience surrounded by nature, "La Turiana" estate is worth every peso.

review_1_text: You can spend a lovely two to three hours here learning about coffee, enjoying the views, and taking in the atmosphere.  Please note, this is one of the few places in Colombia where bug spray was actually useful to have.  Apply liberally.  The staff is friendly and very welcoming.
review_2_text: The coffee tour was super interesting, and Jeffrey was an excellent guide who explained everything very well in English. Everyone was very friendly and attentive. It was not overcrowded with tourists at all, making it a very traditional farm that can be recommended without hesitation.
review_3_text: This was our first coffee tour and we loved it! Jeffrey did our tour in English and was so friendly and knowledgeable. He taught us so much and answered all of our questions. We did a tour through the coffee farm and even harvested and got to process our own beans! After the farm portion, we met Jurledy in the cafe to learn about coffee tasting. She was also fantastic. She taught us the best way to grind and brew coffee, as well as what to look for as far as quality at home.
review_4_text:
The whole experience was absolutely. We were afraid as the tour was made by young girls but they turned out to be super knowledgeable and speaking GREAT English !
I would DEFINETLY recommend to come
Here to discover authentic coffee.

The only thing I would have like to
Watch is the roasting of the coffee but they do not have….
review_5_text:
THIS IS THE MUST DO COFFEE TOUR!!
From start to finish it was amazing! The view was incredible to take beautiful pictures. There are beautiful horses and dogs around giving it the full coffee farm experience. Our tour guides were amazing! They were  so nice and personable. You get the full coffee tour experience they dress you in ponchos and hats you get to pick and taste raw coffee beans see the whole process and history of coffee.  Then they show you how to properly brew coffee and how to tell the good quality coffee from the bad quality. I went with my family and we learned soo much, we were so impressed with the tour!! . What I love about this is that the tours are done in small groups so it feels more personal and you get the full experience! Overall amazing experience and a must in Quindío !!!!

opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text: While the weather didn't cooperate for my trip to Nevado del Ruiz (Snowy Ruiz) as it was foggy and rained, it was still absolutely stunning. My English speaking guide Valentina was outstanding, stepping in to translate for me when my limited Spanish wasn't enough. I couldn't have asked for a better guide (muchas gracias, Valentina!!). Shout out to Jhon our driver as well! Ending the day at Termales el Otoño (Hot Springs) was the icing on the cake and JUST the R & R I needed! Thank you to everyone at Cattelya, you guys were fantastic!!
review_2_text: amazing tour
review_3_text: We did the Nevado del Ruiz + Thermales tour with Gabriel. Great day, the national park is a must! Gabriel was very dedicated, spoke English well. We are taken to a place where a very good lunch and dinner with traditional Colombian food is served. Guillerman the driver was very good at navigating the winding roads. We received great service from the agency, having booked the tour at the last minute. Quick response on WhatsApp. I recommend!
review_4_text: For those who want a summary: An excellent day trip to the snow-capped Santa Isabel, it is worth paying for and experiencing. For those who want the details: we had excellent customer service, they informed us in advance of the departure time (4:30 am), we began the journey along a rural road for 45 minutes and had breakfast (where Hernán, very friendly people and delicious menu), then we continued 2 hours along the same road until we reached the entrance of PNN, the driver (Ferney) was an excellent person and we take our hats off to the way he handled such complex topography. The guide (Alexander Largo) was also excellent, not only for his very professional work, but for the care he took with us, it was important to wear 3 layers of clothing, good grip shoes and follow all the recommendations, the appropriate break for the walk. The experience of reaching the beginning of the glacier is simply spectacular and unforgettable (thank you for that). On the way back, lunch was sensational, soup made with wood!! We thought it was very cool that they give work to the people of the region with this type of services. We arrived again at 4:30 pm (12 hours in total) and according to our guide it went well for us :D Don't stop going before we have no glacier to visit and finally it is one of those places that in life you have to know, admire and take care of. The tour with Cattleya is highly recommended, we hope to return ;)
review_5_text:
We took a tour to Mt. Ruiz, and it was truly a fantastic trip.
Paulo is very knowledgeable about the flora and fauna and gave us many interesting insights, including into the history of the landscape.
The tour included breakfast and a hearty lunch.
The driver drove extremely sensibly (which is not a given).
We felt very well looked after by Paulo. He also speaks very good English and was able to explain everything to us in a way that was easy to understand.

name: Finca Buenos Aires Coffee Tour & Coffee Shop
address: 631028 Vereda llano grande finca buenos aires, Salento
opening_hours: Monday: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM|Tuesday: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM|Wednesday: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM|Thursday: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM|Friday: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM|Saturday: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM|Sunday: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM
review_1_text: Finca Buenos Aires near Salento is an incredible experience! The coffee tour was both fun and educational. We had the chance to pick ripe coffee cherries, plant our own coffee tree, and learn about the entire coffee-making process. The guide was fantastic—very knowledgeable and passionate about coffee and the farm’s history. The finca is set in a stunning location with breathtaking views of lush green hills. After the tour, we enjoyed some of the freshest coffee I’ve ever tasted, accompanied by a delicious local snack. If you're near Salento, this is a must-do experience!
review_2_text: We had such a lovely tour with Philipe (Pipe) this afternoon. He taught us everything about the process of making coffee and his English was incredible. Thank you for having us, we highly recommend a tour in Finca Buenos Aires!
review_3_text: Very interesting coffee tour, they give you some stuff to dress up in which is fun, you learn a lot about the coffee, you get to pick some coffee. We then got to try some and it was really good! They also sell the beans there. Includes a little snack, drink and of course a coffee! Very much recommended!
review_4_text: Amazing tour of the finca. Our guide Juan Manuel was very knowledgeable and fun. We walked around the plantation, picked coffee beans, learned about the whole procedure and tasted the coffee. I absolutely recommend the experience!
review_5_text: Visiting the coffee farm was an incredible experience! We learned so much about the coffee-growing process, from the cultivation of beans to the art of brewing a perfect cup. Our guide, Anderson, made the tour unforgettable. He was not only friendly and welcoming but also shared his knowledge in such an engaging way, giving us valuable tips on how to choose high-quality coffee. This is an experience I’d highly recommend to any coffee lover—it truly deepened our appreciation for every cup!

review_1_text: Food is delicious, although a bit pricey for Colombian standards. Chorizos are amazing
review_2_text:
There are places that, like old stories passed down through generations, hold within their walls a kind of magic that is difficult to explain but impossible to ignore. Parador de Don Julio in Santa Rosa de Cabal is one such place—a retreat that stands timeless amid the whispering guaduales, offering respite to travelers and locals alike. It is not just a restaurant but a sanctuary where time slows, and the senses awaken to the simple joys of life.

We arrived on an evening heavy with the perfume of the mountains, the air thick with the memory of a recent drizzle. The moment we stepped inside, we found ourselves enveloped by an atmosphere that was neither ostentatious nor overdone—just perfectly balanced between rustic charm and effortless efficiency. It is a place where everything works, where each detail has been carefully thought out without the need for embellishment.

The menu read like an invitation to indulge in flavors that spoke of tradition and home. The baby beef, tender and rich, carried the unmistakable scent of wood-fired perfection, each bite a reminder of meals that stretch long into the night, filled with conversation and laughter. The fillete de pollo, juicy and cooked just right, seemed to hum with the warmth of an old kitchen where hands have known the craft for decades. The chuleta de pollo, crisp on the outside, tender within, had that golden touch that only patience and care can produce. And for our littlest companion, at just 15 months old, they had something too—because here, no guest is forgotten, and no appetite goes unfulfilled.

Beyond the food, there is something ineffable that lingers at Parador de Don Julio—the kind of place where you come for the food but stay for the people. The staff moves with an ease that speaks of deep familiarity, as if they were born into the rhythm of hospitality. Their smiles are unforced, their attention to detail precise yet unintrusive, as though they have mastered the delicate art of making you feel at home without ever overstaying their welcome.

And then, there is the landscape. Just beyond the tables and the laughter, a path winds through the guaduales, their slender green bodies swaying like old souls caught in a slow waltz. This is a place where you can wander after a meal, letting the soft rustle of leaves accompany your thoughts, allowing the stillness of the land to press gently against the hurried parts of your mind. A bar stands at the ready, too, for those who wish to extend their stay just a little longer, sipping on something strong while the world outside fades into twilight.

Parador de Don Julio is the kind of place you visit once and, without realizing it, begin planning your return before you even leave. It is a place that is not just about food, nor just about service, nor just about ambiance—it is about all these things, woven together into something whole, something that lingers. And so, we will come again, and then again, because some places are not meant to be visited just once; they are meant to become a part of our stories, retold time and time again.

opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text: Our first part of our trip to Colombia was organized by Eje Cafetero. It was amazing! Valentina is really kind and all the activities are a great experience. Especially the coffee farmer is an experience that I will never forget in my life. I recommend everyone who goes to Colombia to take this experience.
review_2_text: Tremendous experience!! They completely exceeded expectations. The guide Valentina is a loving person who has a very nice and powerful tourism project, since all the places visited are done in conjunction with farmers in the sector, so apart from having a great time and learning from their traditions, you are supporting the local culture. From day one when I made the reservation, they were worried about me, since I visited them from Chile, they guided me to plan my trip and until the moment we said goodbye, they were always willing to help 😁 I will be eternally grateful! There are many things that I liked about the tour, but the ones that stand out the most are the experience of the coffee farm, the trip in marranitas, the preparation of panela, the camping on the banks of the Cauca River with those beautiful skies, the hidden waterfall to cool off, visiting colorful and very cultural towns and above all the meals that they have prepared every day, very natural and delicious. If you really want to learn about the Colombian peasant culture you have to live this experience. I won't continue telling things so that it can be a surprise, but there are more very entertaining activities. I traveled alone and met beautiful people who made the tour very pleasant, greetings to them if they see this message, they are invited to Chile 😁🇨🇱🇨🇴
review_3_text:
An unforgettable experience on the coffee-growing route of the rural route! We learned how to make arepas, learned about the coffee process, explored the coffee paradise, made panela, and rode the marranitas (small rounds of bread). 💜

But the most special thing was the typical Colombian food they cooked for us and the excellent service we received. Thanks to the coffee-growing team for making our trip an unforgettable adventure!
review_4_text: The country route is wonderful. The guide, Valentina, is a great person. The peasant route project is not only a tourism project, it is a social project where they have been empowering the peasant families of the axis, promoting and dignifying their work. One feels very sheltered with each of the families, learns the work involved in bringing that food to the table and is amazed by the multiple landscapes and dishes that are enjoyed along the route. I highly recommend this experience; I consider that it is suitable for all types of travelers, whether you travel alone or with someone.
review_5_text: I'm sharing a bit of my journey with you. I tried to put few photos. But it was definitely one of the best tours I could have taken. I will definitely take it again, a thousand times over. You connect with nature and the people at every home we stayed at were so lovely. I have no complaints, I can only recommend it if you're traveling to Colombia or are currently there. Don't leave without checking out and taking this rural route, which has a wonderful history of how it was formed and the people who contribute to it are just the same. I loved every second. ❤️

review_5_text:
I visited the National Rice Park motivated by an interest in rice culture and the opportunity to explore a new place as a family. The park has potential, but currently has several areas for improvement.

*Location and Access*:
The park is located in the municipality of Alvarado, on the road to Piedras; close to the main Ibagué-Mariquita road (here there is a billboard at the entrance to the municipality of Alvarado that helps identify the place. However, the signage from this point could be clearer). There is parking for around 25 cars.

*Attractions and Activities*:
The main attraction is a wagon tour pulled by a tractor that includes visits to the museum, mills, crops and a river where it is possible to enter. However, this service is limited to certain times (10:30 am and 2:00 pm) and depends on having at least 10 people to perform it. I recommend visiting in a group to guarantee this experience. Additionally, there is a swimming pool, games area (table tennis) and hammocks to rest, although these activities are not very innovative. The park also has accommodation.

*Positive Aspects:*
I highlight the farm for its abundant trees and the friendly attention of the staff.

*Negative Aspects:*

1. The food, although good in taste and presentation, did not seem fresh and some products seemed to have been reheated several times.

2. Problems with insect control: there were many mosquitoes and flies.

3. The pool was dirty, with branches, leaves and insects floating.

4. An unpleasant smell around the pool, like accumulated water or shed water.

5. Lack of clarity and promotion of services, making it difficult to fully enjoy the main route.

6. If the park is called "National Rice Park," more activities related to this product could be included, such as gastronomic or educational experiences, and even selling rice.

*Quality-Price Relationship*:
The entrance fee ($16,000) is reasonable if you use the pool, and the tour price ($77,000, including lunch) would be fair if it were guaranteed to take place. However, the dining experience needs improvement.

*Recommended Duration*:
If you only plan to enjoy the pool and have lunch, 3 hours is enough. If you include the tour, estimate around 5 hours.

*Would I go back?*
Not for now. Perhaps in the future if the aforementioned aspects can be improved.

review_5_text:

The entrance fee is around six US dollars for adults at the time of this review. Children and the elderly pay a lower fee. There are on-site shops for swimsuits and other accessories at reasonable prices.

It's usually crowded during weekends and holiday seasons (Easter week in Colombia, mid-late June, early July, mid-October, December), not so much during weekdays.

The service in general was good, however; We had a problem with one of the girls since we requested a glass of hot water for a medication and she told us no (it was 9:30 p.m.) In that sense, I think it is important to clarify to the guests the schedule for attending to any type of requirement, since there is no access to a kitchen and there are no stores nearby. Regarding the rooms, the cabins with shared bathrooms are really narrow, so take that into consideration before going. Maybe it's a clarification that they give you via WhatsApp but it doesn't hurt to keep it in mind and request photos of the space.
Monguí's transport routes pass right in front of the cabins so it is perfectly accessible.
review_5_text:
A finales de septiembre de 2024 se nos quedó una cobija en el lugar. Al percatarnos del olvido nos comunicamos para preguntar si la habían encontrado. Efectivamente la señorita me envió una foto de la cobija y le pruguntamos si había algún inconveniente de enviarla a la ciudad de origen con pago contraentrega, a lo cual accedió sin problema.

Le envié una dirección y nunca nos confirmó el envío. De igual forma fuimos conscientes que no era su obligación y de alguna manera fue error nuestro haberla olvidado. De todas formas, a los tres meses vuelvo a escribir a la señorita del hospedaje para saber por la prenda olvidada y no recibí alguna respuesta.

La semana anterior ya teníamos 5 meses de haber visitado el lugar y decidimos aprovechar el domingo libre para viajar a Monguí y aprovechar la ocasión de recoger la prenda olvidada. Le escribimos dos días antes a la señorita y nos pidió una foto de la prenda, la cual reenvíe la misma que ella había enviado cuando reportamos al hospedaje el olvido de la prenda.

Después de avisar que íbamos a pasar por la prenda no recibimos alguna respuesta. Sin embargo, el domingo al llegar a Monguí nos acercamos al hospedaje y el personal presente no sabía nada de la cobija y respondieron de manera negligente que seguramente las personas de aseo la habían tomado.

Muy mala experiencia en ese sentido que denota un servicio al cliente deficiente y negligente. review_1_text:
The battle of the Vargas swamp was one of the most significant battles in Bolivar's campaign to liberate Nueva Granada. The best English language account of this campaign, including a thorough description of this battle and with a focus on the British contribution (but also offering a good general description) is Ben Harper's "Conquer or die!", the motto of the British Legion.

As for the museum itself. It's worth a gander, but is also a bit neglected. There are limited displays and limited interpretation, not helped by poor lighting (several non-working lightbulbs).

Nice view of the monument across the road.
review_2_text: A very historical place in Paipa on a rural setting. The place is very important in Colombian struggle for independence. The museum here has actual records of the letters and the artefacts related to the battle. The place is very well maintained and the place is extremely clean as well. Quite a few food options available in decent restaurants nearby and a lot of artesanal shops are also available nearby.
review_3_text: In this House museum they tell the story related to the battle of the Vargas reservoir, which refers to a historical moment in Colombia. Admission costs 3,000 pesos, and there is a guide who explains general aspects of the battle, the house, and other important information such as the works or paintings. We were informed that during seasons such as Easter or the first week of January it is open every day but in the rest of the year it is open on weekends, apart from that it is also open some days in August and one week in October which is the holiday season. Highly recommended place to learn about the history of Colombia
review_4_text:
Admission costs 3,000 for the year 2024. I find it an interesting place if you enjoy graphic history. I think they could invest more in the maintenance of the place.

From one of its balconies you can have a panoramic view of the Pantano de Vargas monument.
review_5_text: Excellent to know part of the history of our country...

name: Páramo de Ocetá
review_1_text:
we (european backpacker couple, average fit) did this hike completely independently starting and ending from Monguí. we used the free offline maps called "organic maps" and always followed the trails towards "La caja del rey" then continued all the way to the end of the marked trail where we found a lovely waterfall and loads of beautiful flora (lupinos and frailejones / see photo attached)!!

from the main-square in Monguí to the waterfall (photo) it took us almost 4h walking. we walked slowly, with many stops. returning back took about 2h. along the way closer to the top we only saw one farmer working on his field very far away, no one else. we climbed two very low fences.

overall it was a fantastic hike with very unique landscape!! weather can change in seconds between sunshine, rain, hot and cold. trails are mostly in good condition. towards the top there is a section where the bushes and trees are very dense for maybe 200m - but the trail on the offline maps is always correct in case you're in doubt where to go. we were very happy to do this without a problem independently and completely free of charge.
review_2_text:
So, full disclosure. I am a Colombian and really enjoy traveling my country and its culture. I do not support the always-ask-for-personal-data-policy that many of my countrymen are used too.

Now, I went to Mongui and stayed camping at a place called Hospejada Las Cabañas, I managed to get a hold of the owner's telephone number beforehand, Elkin, and he had arranged everything before we got there. He was really helpful and full of information about the town and its historic roots.

we stayed the first night and woke up really early to go hiking to Paramo Ocetá, it is a beautiful place. it is one of those places on the planet that just takes your breath away, the trail was easily visible and took us around to see several landmarks, so, that was great.

In the other hand, and this is where my complaints begin, the logistical setup was poor at best, we left camp at 6 in the morning and had to wait almost an hour so the other part of the group would join us. So, you could imagine an hour waiting in a cold climate is not too comfy. besides, there was no actual waiting place or anything, just at the edge of the Paramo, rough terrain all around.

the guides were Elkin's daughters, the eldest being 23, they knew their way around pretty well but lack the confidence of actually being a guide, they did not speak another language than Spanish, they were very vague in the details around historical events. they tried to provide information about the local vegetation (there were amazing paramo plants). they failed to mentioned or point out at interesting local spots and were unable to provide further details about the Paramo's current events (supposedly there is this dude who is taking a hold of the Paramo, I am guessing, by force)

Now, when we were coming down the mountain, I went ahead of them, there was a couple of people who were very slow walkers, so we pushed through. And this is my biggest complaint, we ran into this guy, who btw did not present himself or carry any official ID or anything. he was dressed like a local man. The dude, who we later found out was the official paramo keeper and worked for the mayorship of the tow, was very rude to us from the beginning.

So I respectfully declined to provide my data to him and his piece of paper, to which he was very altered, he then when on to literally push me and grab a hold of my jacket, stating that I was not allowed to do whatever the hell I want because the Paramos was his and not mine to walk without a guide. I calmly asked several questions, like who he was, what was his name, what type of association was he affiliated with. He declined to answer any of them. He then proceeded to call the police, I asked him to put me through since I wanted to speak with an identified local authority, finally, and because I just had it with this guy, I wrote some gibberish in his piece of paper and moved on. He kindly proceeded to yell at the top of his lungs that I must never come back to the paramo.

so, after an amazing walk, not so hard by the way, to those who like a challenge, I had this experience with a local. I asked around the park and to kind Elkin and he told me about the paramo keeper position and that the guy is a public servant. I presented an official complain at the tourist office.

So, in summary, go there, hope you find people like Elkin. Don't pay for the guide, is not worth it, the walk is pretty straightforward and, as I said before, they do not add up that much to the experience. And finally, beware of the Paramo Keeper, who is just the worst.
review_3_text: It's really good. review_1_text:
we (european backpacker couple, average fit) did this hike completely independently starting and ending from Monguí. we used the free offline maps called "organic maps" and always followed the trails towards "La caja del rey" then continued all the way to the end of the marked trail where we found a lovely waterfall and loads of beautiful flora (lupinos and frailejones / see photo attached)!!

from the main-square in Monguí to the waterfall (photo) it took us almost 4h walking. we walked slowly, with many stops. returning back took about 2h. along the way closer to the top we only saw one farmer working on his field very far away, no one else. we climbed two very low fences.

overall it was a fantastic hike with very unique landscape!! weather can change in seconds between sunshine, rain, hot and cold. trails are mostly in good condition. towards the top there is a section where the bushes and trees are very dense for maybe 200m - but the trail on the offline maps is always correct in case you're in doubt where to go. we were very happy to do this without a problem independently and completely free of charge.
review_2_text:
So, full disclosure. I am a Colombian and really enjoy traveling my country and its culture. I do not support the always-ask-for-personal-data-policy that many of my countrymen are used too.

Now, I went to Mongui and stayed camping at a place called Hospejada Las Cabañas, I managed to get a hold of the owner's telephone number beforehand, Elkin, and he had arranged everything before we got there. He was really helpful and full of information about the town and its historic roots.

we stayed the first night and woke up really early to go hiking to Paramo Ocetá, it is a beautiful place. it is one of those places on the planet that just takes your breath away, the trail was easily visible and took us around to see several landmarks, so, that was great.

In the other hand, and this is where my complaints begin, the logistical setup was poor at best, we left camp at 6 in the morning and had to wait almost an hour so the other part of the group would join us. So, you could imagine an hour waiting in a cold climate is not too comfy. besides, there was no actual waiting place or anything, just at the edge of the Paramo, rough terrain all around.

the guides were Elkin's daughters, the eldest being 23, they knew their way around pretty well but lack the confidence of actually being a guide, they did not speak another language than Spanish, they were very vague in the details around historical events. they tried to provide information about the local vegetation (there were amazing paramo plants). they failed to mentioned or point out at interesting local spots and were unable to provide further details about the Paramo's current events (supposedly there is this dude who is taking a hold of the Paramo, I am guessing, by force)

Now, when we were coming down the mountain, I went ahead of them, there was a couple of people who were very slow walkers, so we pushed through. And this is my biggest complaint, we ran into this guy, who btw did not present himself or carry any official ID or anything. he was dressed like a local man. The dude, who we later found out was the official paramo keeper and worked for the mayorship of the tow, was very rude to us from the beginning.

So I respectfully declined to provide my data to him and his piece of paper, to which he was very altered, he then when on to literally push me and grab a hold of my jacket, stating that I was not allowed to do whatever the hell I want because the Paramos was his and not mine to walk without a guide. I calmly asked several questions, like who he was, what was his name, what type of association was he affiliated with. He declined to answer any of them. He then proceeded to call the police, I asked him to put me through since I wanted to speak with an identified local authority, finally, and because I just had it with this guy, I wrote some gibberish in his piece of paper and moved on. He kindly proceeded to yell at the top of his lungs that I must never come back to the paramo.

so, after an amazing walk, not so hard by the way, to those who like a challenge, I had this experience with a local. I asked around the park and to kind Elkin and he told me about the paramo keeper position and that the guy is a public servant. I presented an official complain at the tourist office.

So, in summary, go there, hope you find people like Elkin. Don't pay for the guide, is not worth it, the walk is pretty straightforward and, as I said before, they do not add up that much to the experience. And finally, beware of the Paramo Keeper, who is just the worst.

review_1_text:
A house by the lake has always been my dream.
Here in Colombia I have found absolute paradise:
The guesthouse in the Xieti Nature Reserve is located directly on Lake Tota - a high Andean wetland surrounded by páramos!

The place is fully sustainable: rainwater is harvested for house consumption and the domestic water outflow is filtered by using natural green filters.

I also learned a lot about further sustainable projects that Felipe (from NGO Fundación Montecito) runs at this wetland area: for example planting native trees grown from their plant nursery or educate the people to raise awareness how important it is to protect and preserve the wetlands.

I highly recommend this place!
review_2_text:
Xieti is one of my favorite places around Lake Tota. The owners Felipe and Juanita were incredibly hospitable and knowledgeable of the region. During my stay, I "adopted" a plot within the reserve to plant native trees, which contributes to the ecological restoration of Lake Tota. I'm excited to see updates on my little "forest" for years to come! Overall, I really enjoyed my stay here and would highly recommend it to anyone! Thanks again!

-Casey
review_3_text: Xieti is a wonderful and charming place. When you are there enjoing the sun rise, it is time to feel the thge wonder of the nature.  Xieti's cabin has been coceived to provide what you need in this wonderful place.  For me, it is important to have comfortable bed, clean bathroom, hot water and some others that you find charmingly intalled, always respecting the environment and nature.  Mountain hikes, local people interaction and quiet (if you want), as well as nice bird observation is possible there.  Return to this place is in my hearth all the time !!
review_4_text:
Xieti is a wonderful natural reserve and the perfect place for someone who feels the need to disconnect from society and connect with oneself and nature. The house is located just next to the lake and you have an amazing view over the lake, especially at sunrise if you are like me and like to get up early! If you are lucky you will see clouds forming and dissolving as the sun rises with a golden tint.
The house is beautiful and it has everything you need. The beds are comfortable, the kitchen is well-equipped, there is a hammock... and a fireplace! What more could you want? We would like to thank Felipe & Juanita who were great hosts during our stay. They explained a lot about the work they do to conserve the flora & fauna of and around the lake (Great job!!) and also gave us many tips on what to do around the lake and surroundings.

PS. The lake is not as cold as they say it is - You can go for a swim!!
review_5_text: The landscape around lake Tota is astonishing and unique, as is the whole region Boyacá.  You will find calm and peace there in this rural flora and fauna. I especially enjoyed hiking to the local beach, playa blanca. You'll be able to meet locals as well as tourists there, it's a popular sight. The hostel itself has a great view and the furnishings is modest and beatiful so you'll have just everything you need. I really enjoyed Xieti,  also because the owners are very caring people and gave a lot of recommendations.  Also, don't forget your sunscreen,  very important!

name: Posada Rural Mundo Silvestre
review_1_text: The Mundo Silvestre Rural Inn hides a culinary secret, offering not only a relaxing spot for tourists looking for a natural experience, but also for those who enjoy ancestral family recipes. This inn has a restaurant open to the public on Sundays. Its specialty is traditional soups, stewed oxtail, tongue in sauce, braised beef flank steak, trout in sauce, and chicken breast. We had the opportunity to enjoy a delicious wheat cuchuco (a type of stewed oxtail) and a delicious stewed oxtail. This place, with its delicious food that showcases Cundiboyacense recipes, is well worth a visit.
review_2_text: A wonderful place, good service, good food and affordable prices. They have wifi and you can work while your children play in the recreational spaces. Lunch was spectacular.
review_3_text: Excellent place to share with the family and have contact with nature, we spent quality time, delicious food and at a good price.
review_4_text: A wonderful place, an incredible view of the lake and the countryside, it is a very comfortable and beautiful place, it has top quality attention from its hosts, its food is exquisite, it has everything from executive dishes, breakfast and dinners; If you are looking for a place like home and well located from the tourist sites of Paipa, this is the place, highly recommended.
review_5_text: If you are looking for a place where they welcome you like your old friends, where the food is delicious and everything is very clean, then this is the special place.  It is very close to the ITP Paipa (Thermal Pools), you go up a small hill and you arrive, you can see the city and breathe fresh air.   This lunch is like traveling back in time when you could eat a soup with natural products.  Thank you all very much, Luz Marina, Willian and grandma.  A delicious Cafe.

review_1_text: Worst experience of my life, malo, haram!! No selfrespecting libanese/Arab restaurant would service such a bad aubergine dish: not soft and smooth, but only aubergine skins hiding under cheese and tomato sauce. Another bad: no clean kitchen, i had to run to the bathroom when i came home
review_2_text: Excellent food, good falafel, very good veggie/vegetarian/vegan options.
review_3_text: Recommended 1. Lebanese Moussaka: baked eggplant, tomato, cheese, basil, and pita bread. 2. Arabic Dish: Quibbeh, falafels, Indian dishes, almond rice, tabbouleh salad, and hummus and pita bread. Excellent service, so order the Arabic red wine.
review_4_text: Family business, run by its owners. The decoration consistent with the theme of the gastronomic offer. We tried the Moussaka, generous in cheese, and with the eggplants at a good point (well "bled"); The preparation is made in disposable aluminum molds, which, although practical, convey a "takeaway" image that can be improved. The Arabic Dish is equally good, flavor guaranteed with well-selected ingredients. Both dishes accompanied with generous tabbouleh, pita and homemade hummus of excellent quality. As an appetizer, the host offered us Arabic tea in rose water, and for dessert, nammura of good consistency and flavor. The seasoning in general is good, although moderate (paraphrasing the owner: to access a conservative public); and although the usual service is between Thursday and Sunday, the host was kind enough to serve us on a Tuesday afternoon to celebrate a birthday. A pleasant gastronomic surprise within the local offer, which is worth visiting.
review_5_text:
The food is truly local. I recommend the Arabic dish and the flavorful moussaka. The Arabic red wine was delicious, a totally different kind of red (highly recommended). The prices are reasonable.
The owner is of Lebanese origin and serves a homey, Arabic atmosphere.

Each dish was well-prepared and bursting with flavor, showcasing the culinary talents of the kitchen. The ambiance of the restaurant was equally impressive, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere that made our meal enjoyable.

However, the experience was overshadowed by the service, which left much to be desired. It seemed there was a significant lack of communication between the waitstaff and the kitchen. Our orders were mixed up, and we often found ourselves waiting far too long for basic requests. The waiters seemed overwhelmed and were not as attentive as one would hope in a dining setting.

In summary, while Sabor y Sazón excels in food and ambiance, the service needs serious improvement. Better communication among the staff could elevate the overall dining experience and ensure that patrons leave with the same satisfaction that the food provides. name: NaturaLove Glamping Monguí
address: Finca San Miguel, Vereda de Tebgua, Monguí
review_1_text:
I decided to spend some quality time with my family and choosing NaturaLove Glamping Monguí has ​​been the best decision I have made.

The place is very quiet and exactly what we needed. Thank you very much Camilo, we had a great time and I will definitely recommend your beautiful place to friends and family.
review_2_text:
Dentro de todo lo hermoso que tiene el pueblo con su tranquilidad y sus tradiciones, éste glamping le da el toque preciso de comodidad y glamour.
Opciones de desayuno (delicioso), zonas amplias, animales, huerta, todo es de ensueño.
Se escucha como pasa el río desde el Glamping, a 8 minutos del pueblo caminando.
El anfitrión muy atento, está muy enterado de las actividades a realizar y de las diferentes opciones que uno puede tener para poder salir de lo convencional.
review_3_text: A great place to relax in nature. There are also many animals such as ponies and rabbits that you can feed and pet. Wonderful views of the mountains and Monguí. The village can be reached on foot without any problems. There is also a grill on the terrace and the breakfast is rich and very tasty. The hosts are super nice and helpful. We had a great 3 days there with our two dogs. Gladly again!
review_4_text:
The place is really one of the best places we have visited, you find an appropriate environment for you and your partner, for your family, for your friends, they fit everything you need.

There is a farm with many animals to share with the little ones in the house, we had a lot of fun with the sheep, goats, rabbits.

We had a guided walk, free of charge, among many other activities.  We were with family, celebrating a special occasion and they supported us with the decoration and typical dishes.

Overall it was a 10 star experience that is worth living and repeating,
review_5_text: Excellent place to relax and connect with nature, the rooms have everything you need and the service is excellent.

In addition to this, taking the workshops on beekeeping, preparation of Paipa cheese, the traditional Indian Soup and the Permaculture tour are unparalleled experiences in which you learn enormously and spend supremely pleasant moments, which will hardly be found anywhere else. Finally, the rooms are very well decorated, they are spacious, quiet and comfortable, with beautiful views of natural spaces full of tranquility and harmony. Truly, a place worth going and revisiting whether alone, with friends as a couple or as a family! ☺️

name: Health Secretary
review_1_text: Muy mal trabajo de la secretaria de salud de Paipa. En cuanto al manejo de que le están dando al manejo de las termales municipales de este municipio. Pero se evidencia ante todo la mala directriz de su alcalde y el equipo en mención.  Parece que SÓLO en mayúsculas que sólo les interesa recibir el dinero que se obtiene por el ingreso a las piscinas termales. Estuve el 7 de enero de 2024 y me dio tristeza ver la administración que le están ejecutando al respecto. Tanto el alcalde como el equipo de la secretaria de salud no dimensionado que el ingreso de persona sobrepasó la capacidad de utilización de dichas piscinas termales. Primero error graso introducir el espacio de las ventas de boletas para ingresar, generando aglomeraciones innecesarias para ingresar. Y de esta forma ponerle un riesgo adicional en estafó de emergencia de tener un ingreso y una salida diferente. Ahí no contemplan el.plan  de emergencia que están obligados por ley de cumplir. Segundo la capacidad de aforo se desborda la del ingreso. Deberían pensar en estrategias más rápidas, sencillas y funcionales para afrontar el periodo vacacional que siempre se enfrentan durante las temporadas vacacionales del año. Tercero y no la menos importante y creo que es relevante: el problema de sanidad que el turista se debe enfrentar dentro de las piscinas termales, la capacidad de vestidores, duchas y batería sanitarias que el municipio debe implementar para evitar que la demanda supere la oferta de estos recursos que deben de ser de primer de cumplimiento paa operar y abrir al público.  Encontrándose con los sanitarios sin agua y encontrarse con necwsidades fisiologicas en ellos y no poder activar la cisterna porque como lo dijo un funcionario cuando le pregunté ¿cómo abren un pisicina publica donde la bateria sanitaria no tiene agua para descargar los inodoros? Y funcioanro solo me respondió dígalo a la administración que son los que deciden y fui a buscar y no había ninguno de ellos y tampoco los funcionarios musnicipales. Las duchas sin agua para poderse ducharse entes de entrar y después del uso de las termales. Contraten la baterías sanitarias móviles para evitar ese feo espectaculo de los sanitarios literalmente "hasta explotar". Nota que solo les importa es el ingreso que se genera por el ingreso. Y como consecuencia que mala imagen ante las personas que visitamos este sitio para relajarse y obtener algunos beneficios al exponerse al uso de los mismos. Que mal por el Sr alcalde y de sus equipos de trabajo para mitigar esta mala experiencia. Yo si me encargaré de no volver a recomendar el uso de este servicio. Pésimo. Para eso les quitaron a los hoteles este servicio de las piscinas termales, para monolopolizar de forma inadecuada a través de las piscinas municipales. Les quedó grande administrar y darle buena gestión de los servicios que deben velar como entes de control como fueron elegidos. Esta vez mal por Paipa, porque frecuento mucho este sitio. Solo visitaré a Paipa a descansar, pero no usaré ni recomendaré el uso de las termales municipales.

review_1_text:
The Nemocón Salt Mine is a wonderful place to explore the history of salt mining in Colombia while enjoying a unique and scenic underground experience. It’s a great plan to share with family, especially because the entire visit is guided by knowledgeable staff who share fascinating facts about the mine's past and geology.

The tour lasts around two hours and takes you through beautifully lit tunnels and chambers that offer amazing photo opportunities. The lighting highlights the textures and colors of the salt rock, creating a magical atmosphere that feels both mysterious and peaceful.

One thing to keep in mind is that there is no official parking near the mine. Visitors often have to leave their cars or motorcycles on the street or use improvised parking areas, which may not feel completely secure. Also, taking the guided tour is practically mandatory, so it’s important to plan at least two hours for the full experience.

As for pricing, entry costs are generally over 40,000 COP, which may feel a bit high, but the overall experience, the quality of the tour, and the unique location make it worthwhile.
