review_1_text: Unique place for a yoga and meditation retreat. I thoroughly enjoyed the comfortable accommodations, tasty food, and knowledgeable instruction. The surrounding green mountains added to the peacefulness of the whole experience.
review_2_text:
a beautiful space for healing, inner connections...and wholesome eating.

I absolutely loved my stay at the Retiros de la Montaña. The place brings out tranquillity. Loved the yoga/ mediation class and the breathtaking view of the lagoon.

I was there for 4 days and I wish I stayed longer. The retreat I opted for was the general silence/yoga retreat. Communication with Clara before departing for Colombia was smooth. She really cares about your experience and getting into the practice of mediation and reaching your goals. I arrived in the middle of the week and there were others who were already in the midst of their retreat. Clara and Carlos took the time to sit with me on my first morning to tell me about the facility, schedules and discuss my goals. I loved that personal touch and it made me feel at ease and at home.

Facility:
Breathtaking. You have a beautiful view of a lagoon and there are ducks, dogs, and one sheep on site. The cabins where comfortable and clean. The eating and common area had very warm/homey feel to it. THE FOOD was actually the best cuisine I had throughout my trip in Colombia. It’s loco-vegan- you’d get dishes like oatmeal pancakes to local Colombian dishes (my favourite was soup that had corn, potatoes and beans)

Program:
Clara and Juan Carlos invite you to really connect inward and get into the practice of mediation. The schedule included yoga classes, meditation classes, walking meditation and silence time. It’s pretty chill and I loved their gentle approach. The mediation/yoga classes really help you get connected and feel calm. Also, my group had a mixture of Spanish and English speakers and they did a great job giving instructions in both languages!

Transportation:
It’s an hour and half from Bogota airport. Clara helped me arrange for transportation. Franco was super friendly and a safe driver. He picked me up from the airport to the retreat and back.

I decided to extend my retreat by one day and Clara went above and beyond to accommodate me. I also ended up going to a local community event in Sesquile that another retreat goer was invited to. I will definitely come back and the next time I’ll probably take a retreat/local tourism plan.

The people that run this place are just kind, generous and very loving ....you will feel it!

Thank you to Clara, Juano Carlos and the team!
review_3_text: This place is a true respite of peace. review_3_text: We went camping, the place is good if what you want is to rest from the city and be in a quiet place, there are good places to set up your tent, there are grills and places to make a bonfire, the cabins they rent look nice, I will stay in one of them again, the owner is very formal, Mrs. Mercedes is very attentive, we had breakfast and it was delicious and the service was quick, the bad thing was the bathrooms in the Camping area did not have electricity, the other thing was that the dogs that are there were They ate our food such as packages, coffee, sugar, that we had in the tent and they also broke it, perhaps they need to be educated better since there were other people's dogs that stayed there and they never went to steal anything from us, another thing to improve is that they should think about walks, horseback riding or activities for their guests since then there would be more things to do.
review_4_text:
The good: the landscape from the road to the lagoon

Bad:

1/5: Starting from the arrival, we mentioned to Jorge (the owner) that we did not have a car, he told us to get to Suesca and take a bus there but he did not tell us that after 3 in the afternoon buses no longer leave and you must pay a taxi that costs 60,000 pesos. He was not attentive or attentive at all, he is only interested in making money.

2/5: When we arrived we found a place that looks NOTHING like the photos, it is an ugly, neglected place, with junk everywhere, everything is old and the place lacks maintenance and the Glampings that smell musty, are dirty, with cobwebs. The so-called "Games" for children are dangerous.

3/5: When we saw that, we called Jorge (the owner) because there was no one else except Mrs. Esperanza, a woman between 70-80 years old (she is really very old) who was the only one who took care of the place for everything. When we called him to tell him that we were going to leave, he told us to cancel the reservation on Booking and he gave us a discount, we did so but then we realized that by canceling our reservation on Booking we could not qualify later.

4/5: Since we didn't have transportation, we stayed in that place and it was the WORST Glamping experience of my entire life. The telescopes are useless, everything smells bad (damp), the ceiling, the place was dirty, no maintenance.

5/5: When we went out to breakfast, we found other people and oh surprise, again only the elderly woman serving, this man really seems stingy, it's exploitation. The lady must clean, maintain the place, etc.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND IT, DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY.

review_5_text: I can say that the restaurant service is terrible, I have no idea about the food because we were never even able to order, they were "rotating" the menu. review_1_text:
El lugar es increíble para pasar un fin de semana, las cabañas son cómodas e incluyen cobijas térmicas y desayuno súper completo, hay opción de azar en el lugar y el señor muy amablemente nos ayudó a encender la fogata, puedes comprar comida rápida con ellos con precios justos y un buen sazón.
Cuentan con una buena zona de parqueo, gran lugar para volver.
review_2_text:
The place is too nice, it has beautiful views, very good service and too cheap.

If what you want is a complete experience of what it means to camp, this is the place you have to come to
review_3_text: Super mala la experiencia. El lugar que pensamos era, resultó siendo súper diferente. Las fotos la verdad que no muestran mucho del lugar y pueden ser confusas. Cuando llegamos el espacio era muy pequeño para cinco carpas. Estábamos al lado de un risco con ninos de 2 y 3 años así que no íbamos a correr el riesgo de quedarnos ahí. Por último yo aparte mi cupo con la mitad del valor pero al ver que no era lo que esperaba pedi la devolución y me dijeron que solo me daban la mitad. Pero cuando vuelvo a escribir no me responde nada. Así que creo que se quedaron con la plata. No recomiendo este lugar
review_4_text: The people there are super friendly and helpful. Good breakfast. But the service of those who answer through WhatsApp is terrible. They offered us the rental of mattresses but it turns out that they don't rent them on site, that's a lie. It is serious because in Suesca there are not many options for this type of needs, they rent tents or lodgings but not mattresses or mats alone. The bathroom is good, the place is very humble but it is appreciated that the bathroom was clean, it had no bad smells or anything like that at least.
review_5_text:
Extraordinary location that gives a view of the impressive landscape. Changing climate like that of Bogotá.
We never received what we hired for camping, nor the conditions they offered us, but one of the most uncomfortable things was the location of the tents, placed without taking care to remove the stones from the floor, nor the irregularities and slopes of it. If you are counting on good bathroom service, this is not the place to choose.  Try to bring everything you need since everything is rented or sold, such as firewood, shower and grill for firewood.

review_1_text:
Calm camping grounds surrounded by a natural reserve, an always-present chirps of birds, and a creek where you can bathe in a freezing water.

The owner is very friendly, and always gives you privacy you need to feel like you are far away from civilization. If you are interested, he can teach you the history of his finca.

There is breakfast and lunch service, along with coffee and hot chocolate, clean bathrooms, free clean drinking water, cold and warm showers, and a thermal bath.

The only downside to it is the route to get there, get ready for a short but difficult hike up when you want to return to the entrance.
review_2_text:
There are several thermal places but I really liked this one, because apart from being very cheap, sleeping next to the river and being able to cook,... I found the peace and tranquility that I needed, the idea of ​​leaving the city is to enjoy nature and being able to listen to the birds singing, the river and so on.
Well, in these other places you can't even walk with so many people!
Very good attention, Mr. Juan Camilo very attentive to our needs and very helpful.
I recommend it.

name: Termales Agua Hirviendo
review_1_text: Staff makes this place unforgettable. This was our 3rd visit. At 10pm there was no restaurant service but staff assisted us in boiling water for ramen. The cabins are basic. A few years back they had tvs. The sulfur ruined them we were told. The thermal springs are open 24 hours. Yet the area is quiet and you can be sure you’ll have a good night sleep. Its cold so pack accordingly. The sulfur smell is strong but you get accustomed to it. Beautiful when the sky is clear. Best star viewing. Road from popayan to the thermal springs has been paved so the trip is quicker. Definitely recommend.
review_2_text: Very nice place with hot springs but warning that the sulphur really smells. It's very hard to get it out of your hair and clothing. My swimming suit still sinks after multiple washings. The lunch is good too. There were a lot of locals when we went.
review_3_text: Unique place with simple cottages directly at the spring with 24/7 access to the hot spring. At the time we visited the place, two water basins had not be filled. The hot spring experience is like Sauna in Europe and amazing!
review_4_text:
A great place to relax at a very decent price, only 20.000 pesos (as of Jan2K22).
There are several different pools of varying temperatures as well as a natural sauna. Mainly locals and there's a good restaurant too. To get here from Popayan, take a minibus from the bus station (1h, awesome scenery but rather bumpy) to the quaint little town of Coconuco and from there get a mototaxi to the thermal baths.
I fell in love with Coconuco,  the locals are so friendly and they are surrounded by mountains with lush vegetation which makes it out of this world. A must do trip when in Popayan!
review_5_text: I heard it used to be better, but it was kinda run down and we left and went to aguatibido.

review_1_text:
Amazing, amazing place!

Entrance fee (as of July 2022) was 20,000 COP. Lockers cost 2,000 COP.

This place is run by the indigenous community, and they're doing an amazing job. The facilities are clean and plentiful, and there's an air of calm and respect. I went on a Sunday, when it was busy, and I didn't feel crowded or pressed at all.

There are 3 pools and a cold river, as well as cold showers. Two of the pools use natural rock formations as the basin. It's very relaxing and clean.

There is also a mud (lodo) pit, which you can access for free.

The mirada at the very top is incredibly beautiful.

For those coming from Popayán, it takes about 90 minutes. The bus leaves from Barrio Bolivar in Popayan (6500 COP) and goes to Coconuco. From there, you can take a moto or taxi (I was alone and took a moto for 10,000 COP each way. The same driver dropped me off and picked me up, per our arrangement.) Be advised that the last bus from Coconuco (at least on Sunday) is at 5:30 PM. People did tell me the springs are open 24 hrs, tho, which I'm not sure is correct.

For any extranjeros traveling through the Purace region, I highly recommend this local hot spot. It was an incredible day!
review_2_text: Great secluded spot with warm and hot baths surrounded by the mountains. Includes a playground for kids and two restaurants (that don’t open until after noon and close by 5:30 pm). We could stay on the parking lot with our camper van and use the facilities. The road to get there is very rocky and slow going, but doable in 2WD car or van. During the weekend it’s a lot busier with buses coming in from the nearby towns.
review_3_text:
Really nice- not too crowded on a Tuesday. Pools were lovely and clean. Food was great. Don't forget to check out the waterfall!

The mud bath was low on mud (maybe we weren't trying hard enough?) and be sure you arrange to be picked up by your driver if you take a taxi from coconuco. (I don't think any taxis regularly service the area and no numbers were available to call).

Definitely recommend!
review_4_text: Very friendly place! Beautiful.  And they really care about preserving the nature. It's not fancy. But if you want a quiet, chill, and rustic experience, it's amazing
review_5_text:
This place is so nice! There's a waterfall, a mud bath, and a few different hot pools. There owners are super sweet and the restaurant is good. There were not a lot of people when I was there and it's a very beautiful place!

I stayed the night in a cabin which was 60K.

It's on the route if you're travelling between San Augustin and Popayan. Or a good day trip from popayan :) from coconuco you can take a mototaxi to the springs.

review_1_text:
The place is just amazing!!!
There are a couple of swimming pools, from the muddy one to scrub your body to the crystal clear water with small fishes eating your dead skin.
The landscape is also very beautiful, surrounded by mountains and waterfalls, the hot springs even have a small lake to go kayaking with swans and duck. There is also a couple of peacocks.
It's definitely a place to relax and enjoy the day!
Becarful if you are going low season, some pools can be close and there is no restaurant.
review_2_text: Awesome place. The waters are naturals. The water come from the Purace volcano. The entrance costs 22000 COP and you can access to many natural pools with many different temperatures. This place closes at 5 pm.
review_3_text:
The actual place is very beautiful. 3 different hot pools, a mud bath and a crystal clear pool with Garra Rufa fish.
My only wish is to magic away all the idiots that ruin the peace and tranquility by shouting, screaming and jumping in right in front of you with no respect for the nature of the place. Four guys were covering themselves in sunscreen and diving into the fish pool and the guard did nothing about them polluting it for the fish ☹️
review_4_text: Bit rundown, needs maintenance. Value for money I found it very expensive. I would expect better service and better maintained facilities.
review_5_text:
termales are open as of July 4, 2018, but my moto taxi told me that the owner is currently in negotiation with the indigenous community
this week and they may shut again. Highly
Recommend that you call the day of your visit to confirm that they are open.

The thermal springs offer changing rooms and lockers to store your belongings. Bring your own lock for free or rent one for 3,000 COP. The entrance is 18,000 COP. There is food to purchase at the restaurant, but it shut at 4pm. There are signs that say that outside food is prohibited, but at least when we came during the week, there were plenty of people bringing outside foods in. Not whole meals or picnics,
But definitely snacks, drinks, and beers.

At the very top is a more natural (and he coldest) spring with tiny fish that “bite” gently at your feet. Kind of like those crazy fish spas that people pay money to put their feet in haha.
There is a mud pool that is a bit far
From the rest of the polls as well as a concrete water slide. The slide is a little rough, and definitely varies with how fast the water is pumping out at the top. I did it once, but didn’t want it to ruin my bathing suit fabric and the drop off from the slide is quite shallow if you are going fast. On the other side of the slide are five or so more hot spring pools. The one st the very top is the hottest! That
One definitely felt like a real hot
Tub, While the others felt like varying ranges of bath water. As you move closer to the water
Source in the last pool, the water approaches pretty hot temperatures.

Overall, it cost 5,000 COP each way to get there on bus from popayan, 4,000 COP for the moto ride there, and 18,000 for the entry.  Not too expensive for a day of Soaking up the mountain air and  lazing about in some hot springs.

The changing room and bathrooms were well kept. The place wasn’t busy during the week. We were not able to get a moto taxi back, however. We got the number of our moto but the cell service was bad by the hot springs. Fortunately, we hailed the bus back to popayan from the side of the road. You might want to check if the bus from popayan will drop you at the springs directly to avoid the 4,000 COP moto ride there. Our bus driver told us to get off, but it might have just been because he thought we were going to the other hot springs. Ask your driver!

The Chorrito de la Pamba is the oldest still current water supply source in the city and in Colombia, dating back to the 17th century, and is located in the oldest neighborhood of Popayán, the neighborhood of La Pamba, the most surprising thing even after its more than 380 years, is that water continues to flow from it, this water coming from nascent water sources of Cerro de la M or the three crosses (unfortunately contaminated today by workshops and pipes).
This little stream developed along with the nascent city, and it has seen events happen throughout its history.
Popayán is blessed with its wonderful climate and geography, it has been concluded that our wonderful "jets", apart from responding to the artisanal provision of water and favored by this very friendly climate, consolidate a purely Roman criterion, there is no vestige of a more reliable Roman fort than that of Popayán in America.
The Roman fort, Castrum, plural castra, fortress, was a fortification or military camp of the Roman Empire before the 1st century BC. C. Their camps were always built according to a rectangular plan model with two main passes that intersected: the "Cardo Maximus", which extended to the north and south, and the "Decumanus Maximus" to the east and west, which divided the field into four equal parts; The rest of the streets and buildings were parallel to the main ones, which formed a grid pattern.
The castrum was the basis of the model used by the Spanish colonists in America, the "tablero" of 7 blocks of 100 yards-80 meters per side with a Plaza de Armas in the center near a river and a defensible hill, following strict regulations imposed by the Spanish monarchy for the founding of new cities in the New World.
With the arrival of the Spanish conquerors to the Pubenza Valley, this concept of channeling and supplying water began to be implemented both for private properties and public streams, where people came to collect the precious liquid.

The two-hour walk feels short, and exploring the now-inactive industrial facilities is mind-blowing. You should bring your camera or phone with a full battery and plenty of space, because you'll never tire of taking stunning photos with every step!

review_1_text: Greta place🏕️🍃🌳
review_2_text:
A beautiful place to disconnect from the noise and the world in general. It's a very large and quiet place surrounded by nature. The cabins are super nice and very private. Oswaldo and his wife were very kind. It's a self-sustaining place where the cabins run on solar energy, and they have their own crops, cows, etc. Staying here helps contribute to the success of this beautiful project.

Everything is very natural. The stay includes a bottle of sweet wine and breakfast, which is very homemade and delicious. It included fruit, scrambled eggs, arepa (a traditional pastry), cheese, and hot chocolate or coffee.

The road is completely paved, very good, and the place has plenty of parking for both cars and motorcycles.

We stayed at Las Pavas, a cabin perfect for couples, super private, and with a very pleasant waterfall.

Keep in mind that there is no hot water and only Claro signal is available. We don't have Claro, so we were completely cut off from our communication during our stay, but in the end, that only made the experience better.

There's plenty of space to walk around and explore. We only planned to spend the night there, but the stay was an experience we didn't expect.

We were very happy with everything! 😊

Highly recommend coming here to try traditional Popayan foods while you’re in town!

We tried:
-champu (maize drink made with lulo, pineapple, Panela) it was sweet with the taste of cinnamon. The cinnamon is a bit overwhelming. if you don’t love cinnamon, choose one of the other drinks!
-Lulada: made with chunks of lulo fruit, which looks similar to a tomato with a green/orange color. Very tart but highly recommend!
-salpicón payanese: the best local drink! BlackBerry, lulo and guanábano (white tropical fruit). Delicious and sweet!

The small sizes for drinks are tiny, so go for the grande!

Empanadas de pipian: local empanadas made with potato paste and peanuts. They come in an order of 10 and you’re going to want more than one! It sounds like a lot, but they are tiny for empanadas. They came out hot and fresh. It was hard to stop eating them! Served with yummy peanut sauce.

Tamale de pipian: made with corn and the same potato/peanut paste. Served with peanut sauce. It was okay, but the empanadas are definitely better.

review_1_text: This place is excellent for relaxing, sharing with family or as a couple. I found it to be a peaceful, close-by spot with beautiful scenery. The baths have also been enlarged, and the combination has ensured that the water now enters the baths colder and because they are larger, it cools down more. In short, I do not recommend it. THE WORST EXPERIENCE EVER. Regarding the response issued by Turismo Andino, I find it concerning that they don't have a record of the people who traveled to Mompiche from January 8th to 10th and that they can't contact us. The Bird Viewpoint in La Cocha is a true paradise for lovers of nature and bird watching. Located in the idyllic surroundings of La Cocha lagoon, in Nariño, Colombia, this place is a hidden treasure that is worth a visit. From my perspective, it is a must-see destination for any bird enthusiast and for those simply looking for a peaceful and enriching nature experience.

This viewpoint offers spectacular panoramic views of the lagoon and its surroundings, creating a serene and relaxing environment perfect for bird watching. The diversity of bird species that can be seen here is astonishing, from waterfowl such as ducks and herons to majestic raptors that take to the skies.

What makes this place even more special is its commitment to conservation. The local staff and guides are dedicated to preserving this unique ecosystem and ensuring that the birds and their habitat are respected.

In short, the Bird Viewpoint in La Cocha is an exceptional destination to connect with nature, learn about birds and appreciate the beauty of Colombia. If you love bird watching or are simply looking for a quiet place to connect with nature, you should definitely visit this charming corner of the world.

review_1_text: What a beautiful cultural center of the Banco de la República in the city of Pasto, in the department of Nariño. review_2_text:
The Cultural Center of Banco de la República in Pasto, Leopoldo López Álvarez, is a space for encounters with the region's heritage, research, knowledge and reading. The center is in constant interaction with the community of the municipality and the departments of Nariño and Putumayo, to whose inhabitants it offers programs, activities and information management services.

The Leopoldo López Álvarez Cultural Center is recognized as a promoter of culture and education in Nariño, through three fronts of action: the Library, the Gold Museum and musical and plastic arts programming. In the Library you can consult, in addition to the almost 3 million titles that are part of the catalog of the Banco de la República Library Network, a bibliographic selection of 62,000 copies. As part of the Library there is also the Regional Documentation Center, repository of the region's documentary heritage, which has 2,260 materials about the department of Nariño, including books, audiovisual archives and sound records; in addition to some titles from the private collections of distinguished Nariño writers such as Ignacio Rodríguez Guerrero, Alberto Montezuma Hurtado and Emiliano Díaz del Castillo; and from the private bibliographic collection of academic Leopoldo López Álvarez.

In the musical and plastic arts programming, the Cultural Center offers the Nariño community a wide variety of exhibitions of anthropological pieces and artistic collections. In addition, a constant program of concerts, workshops and conferences alternate in its Music Room and Auditorium. For its part, the Nariño Gold Museum rescues the legacy of the indigenous cultures that occupied the department for about 2,500 years, preserving and recognizing ancestral memory through its collection of ceramics and goldsmithing, with the aim of generating processes of conservation, research, analysis and dissemination of cultural heritage.

Juan Lorenzo Lucero
Traveling in time is possible when visiting the Juan Lorenzo Lucero Museum, where a wide collection of pieces from various periods take us to remember the daily life of the Pasto of yesteryear; The places, customs, traditions, rituals, medicines and utensils are some of the vestiges that can be seen.

This Museum was founded on December 11, 1974 by the priest Jaime Álvarez, an Antioquian Jesuit who sought to immortalize the name of one of the most recognized Pastuso religious, Monsignor Juan Lorenzo Lucero.

Inside it preserves works of religious, archaeological and historical art; documents of the heritage of southwestern Colombia and relics of illustrious people who stood out nationally and internationally, among them bishops, priests, writers, poets, musicians, rulers, soldiers and politicians.
Located with a strategic location in the center of Pasto, it is part of the Juan Lorenzo Lucero Foundation, a work of the Company of Jesus. For 48 years, founded by Father Jaime Álvarez, it has provided a place to exhibit representative pieces of the history and heritage of Nariño, but also spaces for culture, training in various topics, as well as the artistic expressions of the youngest and society in general.

It has 5 rooms that the public can visit, the memory room, represents the territorial tensions that our region has experienced but aimed at showing the processes of reconciliation, resilience as well as the commitments to building peace; the art, liturgy and popular devotion room, expressing the strong liturgical and devotional roots of the region that have endured throughout history, highlighting Pasto as a theological city; the regional history room, which through its pieces represents memorable moments and characters in some eras; that of mission men, where the mission of the church and some Jesuits is located in Nariño; and finally the Nariño composers' room, where the visitor will be able to see the artistic wealth of the outstanding musicians and composers of our region.

With the physical reorganization that it has recently undergone, it has been intended that its spaces also be renewed in favor of the service to the Nariño community, especially young people, with this the aim is to provide a space for recreation, entertainment, continuous training in various areas of interest to young people and the entire Nariño society in general, in addition to proposing itself as a meeting space, sharing youth knowledge through words, workshops and various activities.

review_3_text:
To get there, you can take the intersection that connects Mijitayo, the Mayor's Office, and Obonuco. It's a dirt road that leads to the town. It's approximately a three-hour walk at a brisk pace to the entrance of the Sanctuary, or four if you take breaks. I recommend going on a clear day and bringing plenty of water, sunscreen, an umbrella if you want, and some food. Along the way, you'll find many shops along the sidewalks, so if you forget something essential, you'll be able to get it easily. If you have pets, I recommend being careful; there are many dogs, and some of them, especially those at the end of the path, can be aggressive.

As for the location, it's beautiful. You can see different species of birds along the way, along with plenty of open fields and mountainous landscapes, cows, streams, and flowers. Upon reaching the Sanctuary, the path is adorned with many daisies. Avoid cutting them; they add charm to the place. In short, the hike is easy.

As for La Laguna, since entry is prohibited, you can't really enjoy the view. You can climb up to the entrance where you'll find the ranger's house. He leads you into the area to a small viewpoint, where you can't really appreciate the panorama. The lagoon is undoubtedly beautiful, but because many years ago it was used as a trout farm (an invasive species) and people hunted native species, controls are now stricter. Unfortunately, despite doing something good, such as restoring and caring for the area, responsible ecotourism isn't promoted, as it's very discouraging to know you can't enjoy the place. You're only allowed at the viewpoint for 5 to 10 minutes, and the path to the trail that leads to another part of the lagoon is inaccessible. If more investment were made in staff and in raising awareness about caring for the area, it would undoubtedly be a very beautiful park.

review_5_text: There is no signage to walk to the black lagoon. The information varies, due to lack of official information. The Nature Reserve is closed. You can only go up to the forest guard's door. (1 hour 30 minutes walking). From there you cannot see the lagoon. We still do not understand why they close the nature reserve, if they can open it, protect it with a forest ranger and employees, and in the process they can promote conscious and responsible ecotourism.

name: Temple of Saint John the Baptist
review_1_text: Good
review_2_text:
The temple of San Juan Bautista, located next to the Plaza de Nariño, one of the old buildings in the department.
Where you feel small aromas when you enter, and you are dazzled by the fascinating infrastructure that seems to be designed with gold particles in each space, it is a temple that mixes different styles among which are Muslim, due to the way in which the spaces are distributed, on its altar is the mixture of astrological studies that the ancestors carried out, therefore these findings permeate throughout the altar where a most visible and beautiful part is the combination of gold with many eight-pointed suns. Along with numerous works carved in wood throughout the church, this temple was the first cathedral that had grass, but Bishop Ezekiel at that time decided to build another cathedral with a classic Romanesque style, therefore the cathedral of this temple was moved.
However, it is one of the most beautiful that fills the religious culture of Pasto.
review_3_text: Known as the Church of San Juan, it is one of the most representative colonial temples in the city, with a simple but very traditional design. It is located near the center and is an important reference point in the spiritual life of the Pastusos. Quiet space, ideal for praying. Parishioners highlight the warmth of the religious community.
review_4_text:
Here we can find Saint Jude Thaddeus, a disciple of Christ, who has an arrow and a bow and we also find Saint Roch, he is the one who suffered from leprosy and had a sore on his shin and the dog and since at that time the people of that time were people disowned for having leprosy, it was difficult for him to go to the city because they were killed, so the dog went to get food for him.

San Roque is the patron saint of veterinarians

We also found a pulpit which in the past the priest would go up and dictate the sermon but the Latin was renewed after 1968 because the people did not understand anything, having a pulpit means that the church is very old and is very valuable

We can see that on the altar and around the altar we find everywhere The Sun of the Pastures which was the result of observing the stars, the constellations, it is an eight-pointed sun which forms stars.

When the republican armies of Simón Bolívar came to destroy grass, they entered this temple and the people thinking that the armies were going to respect them took refuge here but they murdered hundreds of people inside, women, men and children.
review_5_text:
The Juan Bautista Church, Pasto's first cathedral, is an impressive architectural testimony that dates back to the colonial era. Its infrastructure and design reflect a rich fusion of styles, including Muslim, baroque and neoclassical.

The figure of the Sun of the Pastos, symbol of the region, predominates in the decoration of the church, adding a unique touch to its beauty. However, it is evident that the church requires further care and restoration, as some areas show signs of neglect and abandonment.

Despite its historical and cultural importance, the church remains closed most of the time, limiting its access and knowledge. It is essential to preserve and promote this architectural and artistic heritage for future generations.

address: Km 10 Vereda, Santa Rosa de Cabal
review_1_text:
The place is really amazing. Breathtaking. The waterfalls and the little river crossing around make the visit already worth it.

We went early in the morning and it was not so crowded. At 11am got really crowded.

The pools are not really taking care of. They need a bit more of maintenance. For the amount of money they charge you would expect something better.

People goes inside with clothes and drinks. There are signs with rules but Nobody from the place is controlling them. It is a bit disgusting.

Overall this place is fine, worth the visit just for the place, not for the termales.

Tip: buy the tickets in advance as they are cheaper. But you will still need to queue to get the brazaletes.

Parking: there is a “free” parking in front of the place. They ask for a tip. If you go early, at the time of the first opening, you’ll find place for sure.
review_2_text:
We went in June, and they were a lot of kids. It was hard to relax. This was not their bussiest time.They don't allow you to bring food in. We ordered food which took over an hour for us to get. On a side note, the food was okay. We could have waited or just had eaten their pre-made guava cakes. Those were yummy.

I would suggest going midday since, at this time, it gets dark around 6 pm. We did pre-order our tickets, which saved some time. The line for purchasing tickets was pretty long. I didn't see anyone get rejected, but to be on the safe side, I would suggest buying them in advance.

If your hungry the restaurant outside of this place are great and of course cheaper.
review_3_text: Wow. A secret paradise of waterfalls and tranquility in the Colombian mountains. Amazing food and drinks as well as spa and outdoor experience. Stay an extra day to experience it all.  Book Room 210 and experience a beautiful view and the peaceful sound of the waterfalls at night.
review_4_text:
My stay at Termales Santa Rosa de Cabal was nothing short of magical, a true escape into a world of relaxation, natural beauty, and rejuvenation. Nestled in the heart of the Colombian mountains, this paradise blends breathtaking landscapes, healing thermal waters, and top tier service into an experience that feels like stepping into a dream.

From the moment I arrived, I was welcomed with warm hospitality and impeccable service that made me feel like a valued guest. The staff was incredibly attentive, ensuring every detail of my stay was perfect. Whether it was guiding me through the resort, recommending the best pools for relaxation, or simply greeting me with a smile, their dedication was unmatched.

The thermal pools are the highlight of this oasis, offering a unique blend of warm, mineral rich waters that naturally relax the body and rejuvenate the soul. Surrounded by lush green mountains and the soothing sounds of waterfalls, every soak felt like a healing ritual. The contrast between the cool mountain air and the steaming pools created an invigorating sensation that left me feeling completely refreshed.

Beyond the pools, Termales Santa Rosa de Cabal offers a complete sensory experience. The on site spa takes relaxation to the next level, with massages and treatments that melt away stress. The restaurant serves exquisite local cuisine, with fresh flavors that perfectly complement the natural surroundings. And for those who love adventure, there are hiking trails leading to stunning waterfalls, where nature reveals its most breathtaking wonders.

What truly sets this place apart is the energy, there is something about the combination of the pristine environment, the healing waters, and the warm hospitality that makes this destination feel almost sacred. It is a place where stress disappears, the body is renewed, and the mind finds clarity.

Termales Santa Rosa de Cabal is not just a getaway, it is an experience that stays with you long after you leave. Whether you are seeking relaxation, adventure, or a deep connection with nature, this place delivers it all. I left feeling recharged, inspired, and already planning my next visit.

Incredible experience in this basically resort.
You can order food, drinks, salads, cafés, crêpes, burgers, pizza...honestly anything you can imagine - at an expensive price - and be served anywhere you want.

review_1_text: It's you're considering getting a room on the first floor, don't do it (upstairs double room is great though). The staff is great but expect to hear them clean and talk on the phone as you try to go to sleep if you're on the first floor. The working space is great thankfully and the breakfast is alright and a nice plus. Upstairs room gets 5 stars, downstairs gets 2-3 stars. I really wish I could review individual rooms since the difference is night and day.
review_2_text: This was one of the best places we stayed in Colombia for price, comfort and service. The staff were super nice. They checked us in quick after a long travel day and the bed was soo comfy. Breakfast was good and the hot showers were great. Would recommend.
review_3_text:
I stayed here one night to go to the aguas termales near Santa Rosa. Would definitely recommend this place. The staff was really nice. They gave me directions, got me breakfast, and did my laundry.

The hotel itself is also very nice, with several sitting rooms and a good location. I felt secure in that neighborhood, even at night.

The only thing was the configuration of the room I was in. No windows and the bathroom was tiny. My knees were hitting the wall when I sat on the toilet, and I'm pretty short!

But I would recommend this place.
review_4_text: I stayed here for a night. The room was about twenty five dollars a night with breakfast included. Staff was very accommodating and let me do a late check out upon request. The room was spacious and everything looked brand new. Vibra bonito!
review_5_text: Great little stop in Pereira. Wasn't planning on staying in the city a night but ended up having to. Close to bus station. Didn't expect much on arrival but the rooms were great and priced so good you can't find much better. Breakfast included was a bonus.

name: Hotel San Telmo Pereira
review_1_text: Great place too stay in the center off pereira. Managment.an staff are amazing.aswell if your into art you'll be amazed!!!!!!
review_2_text: Nice place, located right in the center of the city, comfortable and beautiful rooms, very good service and all for a very favorable price, I recommend it 100%, my children loved it.
review_3_text: Excelente servicio y ubicación. Muy seguro para mis hijos
review_4_text: Hotel muy agradable para comerciantes habitaciones confortables es perfecto pues está ubicado en la zona comercial ideal para vendedores viajeros
review_5_text: Simple but very comfortable and comfortable, especially because it has a homely atmosphere where you feel very good and at home...it is very central to everything in Pereira, half a block from the Plaza de Bolivar...24 hour service...I recommend it👌🖒

name: Hotel Plaza Real
opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text:
Good hotel at a very good location. Staff is VERY attentive and helpful, really appreciate it. Gave 4 stars since there was no window in my room, (ask for one who does!) and breakfast was a little poor.
Would return if ever back in Santa Rosa
review_2_text: Very bad experiencie, do not recommend to go this hotel. We booked the suite room and unfortunately there is not hot water plus the hayrdrier did not work and it is located in a very noise street where you can not sleep at night. It is unnacceptable that they offer you a room without checking the things work properly. We informed the recepcionst and instead of apologise, she justified that in this hotel the warm water is lukewarm water. When ordering the breakfast the light was gone and many others guests confirmed that they did not dispose of warm water neither. Finally and most impressed, they do not have any complaint protocol, so they give you a blank sheet of paper where you have to write the complaint. When submitting it, they do not even stamp the sheet with the submitting schedule and hotel name in order you to be able to deliver it to any Colombian consumer complain institute. Disgusting experiencie.
review_3_text: The hotel is ok. You have to request hot water everytime. The soap dispenser is frustrating. There are no windows in the room. It says free parking but that's between 7pm and 7am. They will overcharge you for the extra hours. I wouldn't recommend it.
review_4_text:
This is one of the top hotels in Santa Rosa. I rated it only 3 stars because of three reasons: 1. for the two nights I stayed, the Wi-Fi was essentially worthless. 2. Even on a Monday evening, music from the nearby bar was blasting until 11:00 pm. Strangely, at 7:00 am, Tuesday morning, I was awoken by music seeping through from a nearby store. 3. My small bedroom had no windows or ventalation. Not even a room fan.
I still enjoyed my stay here, and would consider staying again because it was clean and close to the center of town
review_5_text:
The bus to the Termales Santa Rosa hot spring baths passed right in front of the hotel. The hotel is right next to the main square. Staff and management were helpful in making reservations at Termales Santa Rosa. Management spoke pretty good English. They also recommended an interesting cafe staffed and organized by an Association of deaf-mutes a few blocks from the main square. The breakfast was hearty and tasty.

El bus para Termales Santa Rosa pasa justo en frente del hotel. Queda a pasos de la plaza central y de un supermercado. El desayuno estuvo sabroso y rellenador

name: Hotel El Lago 2
opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text: Pretty girls at the desk
review_2_text: A very welcoming place, as was its management. Strategically located next to the park, shops, and restaurants. Good prices. I loved it.
review_3_text: Excelente servicio. Ubicación estrayégica y, a pesar de estar en zona comercial, bastante silente. Impecable en su limpieza. Habitación confortable. Económico. Excelente por el precio pagado. ¡Muy recomendable!
review_4_text: Buena ubicación en los alrededores del parque el lago, ambiente familiar, buena atención, nada de ruido, tiene una cafetería a parte del hotel donde puedes desayunar bien rico, tomar bebidas frías y calientes, un ambiente acogedor.
review_5_text: Un hotel cómodo, pero sin ningún lujo adicional, el parqueadero queda a una cuadra de distancia. Los espacios son aseados y cuenta con agua caliente. El personal brinda una excelente atención.

name: HOTEL AMERICANO CENTER
review_1_text: Very quiet and Peaceable.
review_2_text:
It is a deception that is not the facade of the hotel. The facade that appears is of the Pereira business hotel by Sirgo, it is very nice and neat, I recommend it.

Here I leave you the real facade of this hotel
review_3_text: VERY BAD. TORN SHEETS and I know they kind of change them out there... every three months? If they change them. The shower was cool because it had hot water. HOWEVER, the siphon was clogged and flooded. Old old house. Little maintenance to these facilities
review_4_text: Good prices, well located, you can get everything nearby, from clothes to food, liquor, drinks, the rooms are clean, comfortable beds, the people who work there are very formal and helpful
review_5_text: The rooms are super small... I didn't like the toilet at all, the bathroom was full of cobwebs and then spiders, horrible

name: Gran Hotel Pereira
opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text:
Beautifull old style hotel. In the middle of the center of town. Made in the late 30's and still had the feel of it. Very big rooms and a fantastic shower. Renovated to meet modern standards with fairly good wifi and good Tv service. Good airco and extra service. Very friendly and helpfull staff. Your service, bar etc
To make it 5 stars the breakfast should be better and the windows need an upgrade against the traffic noice. All in all we enjoyed our stay a lot, thank you!
review_2_text: Excellent customer service, Very good breakfast, and rooms. My only concern was one night that my wife and me arrived to the hotel and we were almost assaulted by one of the people asking for money in the entrance of the hotel, next to the lobby. My recommendation for the hotel is having a night porter, because at night the are is dangerous, even arriving in taxi.
review_3_text:
Hotel has a bit of a royalty feel and amazing architecture, especially the spiral path down to the basement where breakfast is served. Room is spacious, clean and comfortable. Staff is helpful and addresses your issues promptly and with care. Great location and walking distance to Bolivar Square and Plaza Victoria. Would definitely consider coming back.

Some issues to declare: (1) There is not really any hot water (was told to leave water running for 15 mins for hot water but i am not gonna waste water!), although shower area is very spacious. (2) Room with street view gets quite noisy with street traffic noise.
review_4_text: Staff was kind and provided great service but the hotel did not meet 4 star hotel standards, especially for the price. For the same price, you could stay at a newer and much nicer hotel in the same area. Everything needs to be renovated, especially the rooms. The staff and service are the only reason I’m not rating this hotel with one star.
review_5_text: The staff and the service they provided was exceptional, and the location is great, but hotel is very antiquated. The room was in desperate need of renovation. The shower alternated between scalding hot and cold. The breakfast was a joke; it basically consisted of three hot plates and coffee, and the last sip of coffee greeted me with a mouthful of coffee grounds. The hotel lost power and did not have a backup generator. Overall, I would not recommend this hotel to others staying in Pereira. The staff/service and location were the lone bright spots.

name: Kapital Suites
opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text: Room itself was great, but the walls are super thin, so you can hear everything. But worse, the cleaning lady entered the room without knocking at 8am, and at checkout when asked what happened, the receptionist just smiled and said it was “an error” without any type of apology.
review_2_text: This place is absolutely lovely. The room we stayed in had everything we needed for a short stay. Both room and bathroom were impeccable.  The staff was very nice and amicable.
review_3_text: Kind of closed off without much light. It has a kitchen but not great for extended stays.  It’s also pricey for the area. Might as well stay at the movich next door with hot tub and pool and good breakfast
review_4_text: Too little lobby, good surrounding areas, nice room, entrance does not look like a hotel, for me it is too much money for this two star hotel.
review_5_text: Very clean friendly staff will stay again

name: La Rivera Hotel
opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text:
A simple hotel, everything is clean although already well used. All employees are very kind, and give an excellent attention.
Covered parking, near the movement of the City center (plaza Bolivar) with lots of restaurants and bars. Easy to reach every place.
Typical breakfast, arepa, eggs, fruits, juice of the day, cheese.
Stayed 4 weeks and liked it. Recommended!
review_2_text: A great place to stay, especially for the price. The staff were very friendly and accommodating, and the rent includes really good breakfast choices brought to your room. The location is great, just walk a few blocks up the hill and you're at the plaza. Has a secure car park beneath the building. Would definitely stay here again.
review_3_text: The best option in cleanliness service and price. Rooms were very clean and well kept. I would stay there again. Easy access to taxis and the center of town.
review_4_text: Great hotel and staff. Very helpful while we where visiting for a large cycling event held in the area.
review_5_text: Not elevators and restaurant service is terrible. Rooms and front desk personnel very professional.

name: Hotel Posada Don Simon
opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text: Don’t stay here ! I’m not even bother by how dirty the floor is, or how much hair I found on the blanket. Its a horrible dirty place in a unsafe neighbourhood. if you are traveling, don’t stay here, it’s more for local to have quick hook up.  the wall are paper thin. you can hear the traffic. people talking in their room. the roof is made from plastic. when it rains at night( which happens pretty much every night in pereira, you will never be able to sleep.) then there is rooster crowing from 4 am every 10 seconds. The shower head was also broken.
review_2_text:
I would not recommend this place at all.

First, the location is at the edge of the center of town, and I was told by the taxi driver who brought us there that the area is not so safe and better to go elsewhere.

Second, the price is too expensive for the location and for the condition of the hostel - it is an hostel and not an hotel!

When I arrived the reception area was messy and dirty, with pieces of cheap carpets covering part of the floors and stair (like the place is under renovation and they cover the floors to protect it).

Also they have a dog running around in reception barking.

The double bed room I ordered was clean but minimal and was way over priced in my opinion.

I didn't stay there of course, but had to pay cancellation fee for the booking.
review_3_text: 2nd time staying here. I have the room with the balcony. They keep this place like new. Great staff too. Highly recommend
review_4_text: Super
review_5_text: I love all.

name: Hotel Paradise del café
address: Cr. 9 Calle 19-25 Detrás del Centro Comercial Bolivar Plaza, Pereira
review_1_text: my room had no view but room was very clean and comfortable. nice big shower. a good place to get some sleep and rest. location was in safe neighborhood, would stay here again. breakfast was included and fulfilling
review_2_text:
Spotlessly clean, great value for money. Provides hot showers, mini fridge, elevator, generous breakfast, helpful staff, shelves and a desk!
The bed is small and hard though. There is a fan but no AC. wifi ok (good but unstable)
review_3_text: Nice hotel, comfy with an awesome shower with hot water. Breakfast was simple but good. Very clean and safe. Only drawback is it’s not safe to walk around after 6pm so definitely use uber.
review_4_text:
Is a very nice hotel, clean and nice rooms, big bathroom, the service and the people are just great, the food is delicious, and the breakfast offered can be tailored from tiny to biiiig.
Is placed in the downtown, near museums, and famous and historical places as the " naked Bolívar square", but in the night the arrival is not so nice, because of where it's located.
Arriving in taxi is the best choice.
review_5_text: Nice hotel in a great location, you can walk anywhere from there. All the staff was great and always made sure you felt confortable. My only complaint is that the doors where so loud, every time someone closed a door you will hear it in the entire floor. Breakfast was good with a lot of choices.
city: Cr. 9 Calle 19-25 Detrás del Centro Comercial Bolivar Plaza

name: Hotel Sueños del Cafe
opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text: Is more a motel than a hotel. Good service though
review_2_text: Very clean and comfortable.
review_3_text: Pereira ! Paradise ! Excellent service !
review_4_text: Fantastic COFFEE ☕ SHOP
review_5_text: Small!

name: Hotel Válcon
opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text: Firt and foremost the most disgusting, horrible just happened to me when I had just arrived to the hotel room after going out at night. There were cockroaches roaming around one of the beds and the floor of the room. Secondly the check in was terrible.  The receptionist said the room that was originally reserved for me was assigned for someone else and they assigned me a random room full of cockroaches.  Thirdly this hotel is right below a full on bar that is extremely loud up until 12 am. Overall the stay has been the worst ever!!
review_2_text: everything great but noisy. hotels need double payne windows and doors. very busy street plus restaurant bar on top floor. i woke up several times. if you're a light sleeper and need your sleep Stay Away.
review_3_text: Close to the square. Clean and friendly staff who were helpful. Left my bag there as well for a night so handy as well. Basic breakfast.
review_4_text: one of the better hotels in Sta.Rosa. there's a convenient rooftop bar/restaurant as well.
review_5_text: Small rooms but the Belgian Waffle shop downstairs is an absolute must.

name: HOTEL TUCAN
review_1_text: It's a good place to stay. Friendly staff. Room are OK.  Has room for improvement. I would recommend it.
review_2_text: Acceptable
review_3_text:
The hotel is well located
normal service
It doesn't have a parking space, it says it has an agreement, but I paid them the same amount of parking anywhere near the hotel, but you still have to pay, normal
The double room smells damp,
A smell is contained, not very pleasant,
TV, normal, only one channel in one of the four triple rooms.
He had very little breakfast, something that they should improve a lot.
review_4_text: The rooms are a bit small, but they're comfortable, have hot water in the shower, and the customer service is very good. It's located in the center of Pereira.
review_5_text: The service is terrible, I do not recommend it at all. The rooms are super uncomfortable. The bed is not a mattress, it is a super bad mat for sleeping. Zero privacy. The people in the other rooms make a lot of noise, listen to loud music, tell the receptionist and she does nothing. The TV does not work. ZERO RECOMMENDATION. I WOULD NEVER RETURN.

name: Hotel Luxor Plaza
review_1_text:
From desk girl basically stole from me
I ask if they have laundry in the hotel and she said not, but they use a  outsider  to do the laundry for the guests...I give her about 10 pieces of clothing which doesn't cost much ..next day I was checking out and claiming my clothing and charges me a little more than I pay for the night in the hotel
150 thousands colombian pesos and I pay for the night 140 thousands pesos....
Thanks God I was coming from USA 🇺🇸 and have the money to pay but that was a robbery.....I was in love whit Pereira, first time there but this was really bad....hope she have diarrhea whit the money she took from me...

I never agreed to any price, that wasn't discussed in that moment...any way...you tock my money and I hope you got a very hard diarrea whit that money
review_2_text: Excellent service. Complimentary breakfast had options and local flavor. Housekeepers are amicable and front desk welcoming.
review_3_text: Room was small and bed was also too small for 2 people to sleep comfortably...
review_4_text: A good choice for a comfortable stay. Doesn't have an elevator or lunch and dinner restaurant. Great service from its employees.
review_5_text: Great experience,  room and location in town. No elevator, but, I needed the exercise.

name: Hotel El lago 1
review_1_text: Nice central cheap hotel with good staff
review_2_text: It is an excellent hotel to rest, excellent attention, good service
review_3_text: Es un sitio cómodo. Lo que más me gustó es su ubicación

name: Hotel Central Pereira 4 18
opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text:
A great place to stay in Pereira. Excellent prices, friendly staff, many thanks to Raúl for his excellent communication in English.

Central location
Clean rooms and common spaces
Great advice
Very comfortable beds
Hot water (not something you find everywhere in Colombia)
Limited use of single-use plastic

There's no free breakfast, but lots of places nearby. And if you want breakfast in the hotel, they'll prepare it for you.
review_2_text: I stayed couple of times at this hotel. The staff is extremely friendly and location is amazing. The place is very pleasant and very clean. I will stay again on my next visit to pereira. Recommended 100%
review_3_text: Wonderful place to stay in Pereira!  The staff is top and very attentive.  The rooms are very pleasant and very clean.  I highly recommend!
review_4_text: Good hotel
review_5_text: Good!!!!

name: Ayenda Optimum Hotel
opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text: Nice
review_2_text: A bad experience with the supposed manager. Three adults stayed for one night and were charged $200,000 for two rooms. However, she arrived in the morning saying we owed her another $100,000 because she claimed we had told her we were two adults, and it was $100 for each person. The rooms were without air conditioning, and in the morning we weren't given breakfast. I don't recommend it, to be honest. The staff was attentive, but the lady negates the good service.
review_3_text:
Very bad service, the lady, the "supposed" manager was very rude, and told us that they were not going to serve us breakfast, why did she mention that she had not served us, being at the table 10 minutes ago....
The rooms were full of mold, the blankets were full of people's hair, stained towels, beds full of dust, our room was leaking water, they just mopped and that's it.

The boy who welcomed us was very friendly.

Just for one night, we swallowed everything, but what happened with the lady was the one that left the experience the most tasteless, so don't come to this hotel, if you want to have a bad experience... Look for other options before getting here.
review_4_text: It is a quiet place with friendly staff and serves a good breakfast.
review_5_text:
Todo muy bien hasta que uno necesita factura, la persona que maneja la facturacion no contesta los mensajes y cuando lo usas para hospedarte por trabajo se requiere que den la factura casi que inmnediatamente, ojala vean el mensaje y solucionen en esta parte.
adicionalmente se me quedo el cargador del celular llame el mismo dia a la persona que tengo de contacto y nunca me contesto el mensaje
quedo atenta

name: Hotel Cataluña Pereira
opening_hours: Monday: Open 24 hours|Tuesday: Open 24 hours|Wednesday: Open 24 hours|Thursday: Open 24 hours|Friday: Open 24 hours|Saturday: Open 24 hours|Sunday: Open 24 hours
review_1_text: I just had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Cataluna. The front desk personnel throughout my entire stay were friendly, helpful, and hospitable. The hotel was very clean and well maintained. My room was large, clean, and very comfortable. The breakfast included every morning was scrumptious. The wait staff and housekeepers were super friendly, professional, and hospitable. I also loved the age and architecture of the building.  Excellent experience. Gracias to the staff at Hotel Cataluna! 🙏
review_2_text: Nice, clean. I only stayed for 2 nights the location is great, and the staff is very professional and kind staff.
review_3_text: Very good price at this area, that staff is super kind. It has no luxuries but it is clean, comfortable and has all necessary for a good rest. The breakfast is good. There are parking lots nearby. I would definitely stay here again.
review_4_text:
The room was very spacious and comfortable, and the staff is very kind and ready to help.
Unfortunately, the Wi-Fi at the 3rd floor was not working, the receptionist tried to fix it but she couldn’t. Also, the shower was a bit tricky, the water was either really cold or boiling hot and at night we could hear people talk from outside, pretty noisy.
The breakfast was really good!
review_5_text: The hotel is excellent located near Plaza Bolivar. The  hotel reception staff  are very friendly. The rooms are large but  some are outdated and the bed  mattress are a bit hard  . Breakfast is simple.  I would be nice if they  could add a fruit plate  to menu.  I would stay again. Good value for what u get.

name: Hotel Condina
review_1_text: Nice, clean affordable hotel. Free breakfast was good and staff at the desk were very helpful especially considering we didn't speak Spanish. They even helped us order delievered food a few times. Good area to stay in the middle of many stores and walking distance from Victoria plaza.
review_2_text:
Hotel Condina.
There are so many wonderful things to write about this hotel. It is centrally located on a pedestrian street. 18th Street is only a couple of blocks from the main downtown site. Plaza de Bolivar is Pereira's main attraction.
The 18th pedestrian Street is full of shops and quality restaurants and bars.There are professional vendors and jewelry shops within reach.
The Condina Hotel is beautiful and super clean. The staff is friendly and very amicable.
I stayed there for a month and always found a friendly smile. The staff service is excellent.
The rooms are clean and the beds are very comfortable. They cleaned my room everyday . But one of the most important aspects of the Condina Hotel is the fact that the pedestrian street is very quiet at night.
It is busy during the day but at night the guests are guaranteed a very quiet night.
I was very happy staying at the hotel.
I think The Condina is the best Four Star hotel in town. The price was very affordable and the reservation went smoothly.
Thank you to the hotel staff for their dedication to service. I will surely be back and stay at Condina Hotel.
review_3_text: I reserved Superior room but got Standard room. When i complained they only found excuses and only offered me by the next day to change the room. The receptionist was not reall helpful. After discussing with the manager i've got at least a discount. Besides that, the breakfast is as desaster.
review_4_text: Great hotel in downtown Pereira. Big rooms,  nice clerk people
review_5_text: This hotel is amazing, I had stay in 5 stars hotels but you know what, how comfortable and how welcome I had feel in this hotel I havent feel it in the most expensive hotels I had stay before. Rooms are big, breakfast is super colombian and taste delicious. IDK but who ever complains about is a morron. I had stay here over 5 times in the pass 6 years and I always be back to this hotel once I have the chance to go back to Pereira

name: Hotel Ayenda Macondo Manizales
review_1_text: Amazing Hotel with the perfect location in a very safe area of Manizales. The hotel has character and is truly special. The staff is amazing and will give you all contacts and information you need to explore the area. In our case they recommended somebody that took us on a private tour to Parque de los Nevados and showed us all the amazing places along Colombia‘s most beautiful road. This was our best day of our entire travel. Don’t miss it 🤩
review_2_text:
Overall, Ayenda Macondo is not a bad place to stay in Manizales but like most places it has its pros and cons.

Pros : the hotel is well located, the staff is comprehensive and helpful and the rooms are basic but clean and comfy. *Please note that the front rooms (overlooking la Calle 20) are quite noisy (it's a busy street + there is a bar right across the street) but the back rooms are quieter (except on weekends where they are also a little noisy).

Cons : the Internet connection is poor and spotty and we did have a to kill a few cockroaches in our room.
review_3_text:
I stayed at this hotel with my mom for four days, and the experience was very good. The staff is extremely friendly, the rooms are clean, there's hot water, and the price-performance ratio is quite good. The interior is very nice, highlighting the essence of coffee-growing regions with its decor and paintings; it has a homey feel.
The place is very close to all the tourist spots, and if you're visiting for medical reasons, buses pass very close by to take you to the clinics.
review_4_text: It was a pleasure to meet the hotel management. They couldn't be more professional, and it's highly recommended for a short or long stay in Manizales. Clean rooms, hot water, and a family atmosphere. Recommended.
review_5_text: Excellent place. The rooms are quite comfortable and private. The workers there are very friendly and helpful, and their service is very good. If I returned to Manizales I would stay here again! Thank you so much :)

name: HOTEL LA POSADA DE DON QUIJOTE
review_1_text:
I searched at least 10 other hotels in the area before deciding in this one. Great service from a friendly team who clean the room meticulously everyday and bring a nice breakfast to your door, which is included in the price of £15 per night. I stayed in Pereira a while so made this my home. :-)
Thanks to Adriana, Piedad, Estefani and all the great staff for making my time in Colombia so special!

‘Mandu’ restaurant across the road does great lunches. Loads of other nice eateries in the area too.
review_2_text: Cheap price, crazy noisy street party outside, but clean and better looking inside than outside :-)
review_3_text: It's a good hotel
review_4_text: Super
review_5_text:
The staff very friendly and attentive.
Very clean rooms, with smart TV, refrigerator.
If you are one of the people who does not mind noise, it is an excellent place, but if noise bothers you, I would not rest since next to the hotel there are discos, tobacconists, bars and this generates a lot of noise.
Otherwise it is a good hotel, reasonable prices and they offer breakfast.

name: HOTEL D'LYON - PÁGINA OFICIAL
review_1_text:
Very good experience in this hotel.
Rooms are very good and the bed is super comfy. It's in a great location as well.
review_2_text: Super
review_3_text:
I made a reservation with Booking, I asked for a room for one person with a double bed with a kitchen, refrigerator and normal bathroom because that's what the description on the page said. When I arrive they tell me that room. It does not have a refrigerator, and if I want one I would have to cancel the reservation and they would give me another room. So I did, then I was surprised that the price increased, they do not have card payments (only cash or transfer, I suppose it is because they want to avoid the commission they charge for the use of the dataphone) it tells me that the use of the kitchen is with an additional payment, the internet is TERRIBLE on the 3rd floor. name: Hotel Movich Pereira
review_1_text:
Unprofessional front desk service by Harold made the Hotel as worse as no star.

NO English document provided during check-in.

Avoid this hotel, if you don’t really want to be treated as stupid tourist here.
review_2_text: The staff here are what makes the stay great.  Juan Carlos greeted us every day offering fantastic advice and local recommendations.  Diego Alexander at the Tipsy Bird played our favorite music and showed us a fun time with generous drinks.  Migel at the pool responded quickly with ice and first aid when our friend's toddler bumped his head.  The young man at the cafe was also very friendly and sweet about my poor Spanish!  Our group also had great spa treatments.  The building and rooms are in need of update and repair.   The restaurant food is decent, but not great , which is what I expect from hotel food/free breakfast.  As for the other reviews regarding speaking English - my very limited Spanish got me by just fine, and we could always find someone who spoke English for more complicated questions.   Manage your expectations about the building, but I would stay again based on the staff alone!
review_3_text:
Unfortunately my experience at this hotel was a very bad one.
Virtually all of the staff do not speak English! So it is a total nightmare when one is attempting to order room service, or even call the reception. One then literally waits 1 to 1.5 hours for simple food requests or even drinks to eventually be delivered.
On arrival the first room we were put in had a very noisy malfunctioning air conditioner! So we did not sleep a wink all night! Next day we were moved to another room! The plumbing system is atrocious so one literally hears the other rooms toilets being flushed all day and night!
We also had the misfortune of having extremely rude and maleducated residents directly next door to us who disturbed the peace day and night to no avail!
The breakfast consists of only very bland and tasteless Colombian foods, even though the hotel caters to a predominantly foreign clientele.
We spoke to the manager three times regarding the noise disturbances but no remedial action was seriously set in place. I’m due to leave tomorrow and to be honest I can’t wait! The only saving grace of this hotel is a team member named Juan Carlos who is extremely polite and helpful and conversant in English. He warmly received us on arrival and was a God send with regard to acting as our translator. It’s a great pity that the hotel is not up to standard as it’s design is very restful.
