address: P249+QJ6, Bosque De Polylepis Sector El Colorado, Hacienda Hoja Blanca
review_1_text: It’s a nice place with a natural reserve and restaurant also free guided hikes, but it is highly overpriced for what it is and the rooms do not have a very luxurious feeling except for the heated blankets (mostly because it is freezing and there is no fireplace). It feels like they are trying to be a highly rated expensive lodge but there is still some work to do. Even the restaurant looks high class but the food is average.
review_2_text: When visiting from the United States with a native Ecuadorian, we spent two nights at Polylepis Lodge and it was such a delight! It has been a great way to connect with nature, relax, pamper ourselves, hike, and enjoy great food. It’s a beautiful destination that’s off the beaten path for tourists, which makes it calm and serene. We did stay Tuesday-Thursday in November. While it was cooler at night, some layers and the boots provided by the lodge were exactly what we needed! The warm jacuzzi in our room heated by fire (that the staff keep in great shape) was such a great, cozy experience. The drive from Quito was also scenic and beautiful. I look forward to coming here again!
review_3_text: This is a wonderful place to visit. The Forest walks is so informative. Is the only place on Earth. You will see this type of forest trees thousands of years old. The staff was over the top. The food was excellent. I highly recommend this place.
review_4_text: Just a breathtaking hotel. Wonderful service and great food. Keep up with the preservation of the millénaire woods.
review_5_text:
This is a wonderful hotel located in the Angel National Park. The hotel is very cosy and the rooms spacious. The staff is excellent and very nice. The spa is great, and really nice after the walks. The guide and tours are wonderful. You learn a lot. The showers however didn't have hot water, but the problem was quickly solved by the staff.
Overall a great stay, relaxing and rejuvenating! We loved the Frailejoles and the paramo, and the Polylepis woods were amazing. Definitely a unique experience.

review_1_text:
I would be happy to give it higher stars, but just wanted to make this post stand out and for awareness.

The owner is kind and the hotel is a great price and clean and nice and I'm very grateful for all this.

The reason I'm giving it a bad review is the sister of the owner who lives there. She was extremely difficult toward me, controlling and cranky. Maybe she just doesn't like Americans or me for some reason, but I tried to be connected with her about the mushroom supplements she sells because I am also more or less an herbalist and also use resihi which they have for sale in their shop.

When I arrived here the owner brother greeted me and was good to deal with and very helpful.

When I came back with my luggage it was her and I could tell she was a fussy controlling older woman but I was patient and polite with her. I asked about the kitchen and they both told me you could use it for the microwave or making teas because they are obviously into that health benefit or so they say.

So the one morning after the night I stayed I woke up early and no one seemed to be awake and I went into the open kitchen to see if any containers were empty and able to be used to boil some Guayusa I had. She appeared out of nowhere shouting saying I need to ask for permission to enter to make tea and that all foreigners do that just not me. I told her I thought she was asleep and that I was allowed to make tea like she had said before.

I told her that her character made me feel stressed and I said sorry and promised to never try to use the kitchen again.

She also entered the room I stayed in and told me to move my stuff from the window sill saying it needs to go in a cabinet (just a roll of tissue paper and a juice).

She also saw me with a banana and kept asking where I would put the peel. Before I had even eaten it, instead of kindly explaining where they put the organic garbage.

She just had a very controlling stressful energy, at least around me and one of the worst I've experienced here in my two years of knowing Latin America.

I would not recommend coming here or returning here unfortunately because of her intensely controlling personality. I didn't feel comfortable at all.

I would love to give it higher stars, but I just wanted this post to stand out and raise awareness.

It is a comfortable hotel at $50,000 per night with the following conditions and services, some additional: bedroom, hot shower sometimes, TV, wi-fi, parking, laundry and common area that they call the viewpoint, it needs "love" to make the viewpoint more enjoyable.

The photos that exist faithfully show what one will currently find. It's a good night, however, there are several buts that explain my rating.

1. The main receptionist is a young woman (very friendly and serves well) who is studying at school, I think she should not be working at this time, for me it is child labor exploitation, I know because I was also a victim. At those ages one does not know the dimensions of what WORK means and what conditions it has, that is, what the "rules of the game" are like, of the game of working.

2. How the people who serve live there, they wake up at 5:30 am to get ready to go to school. I was aware of that context, so I didn't see much of an inconvenience; more care could be taken with turning on the lights and closing and opening doors at that time.

3. The second night they changed the sheet that covers the mattress for a yellow one, very used and old, and they took the sheet off. The first night everything was white and had a sheet. Apparently, one receives a service depending on one's impression. Fortunately there was another single bed next to it and I changed the sheets.

4. The last night they made repairs with drills and next door, at the Agrarian Bank. This was during the night of Sunday and early Monday morning, we couldn't sleep, I stopped to see what could be done but there was no one to do anything. The next day I spoke with the bank manager to make it clear that these are not hours to do renovations and find out what happened. She, the bank manager, was very sincere and acknowledged that they did not notify their neighbors about these renovations. It may be a lack of administration, since the people at the hotel are not coordinated with their neighbors.

Finally I appreciate the service. Greetings.
